Found in the review of #162 (finding 3 in https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/pull/162#issuecomment-6050269233), and older than that PR.

`collect` in `crates/ascribe-fmt/src/files.rs` follows linked folders without remembering which folders it has already visited. A link back up the tree, such as `docs/loop -> .`, makes `fmt` walk the same folders again and again until the path gets too long. With such a link, `fmt --check` lists each file about 40 times, prints ASC123 about 40 times, and reports "41 files would be reformatted". For the same project, `ascribe check` reports each file once.

What a fix needs: remember the canonical folders already visited, as `FileSystem::sources` does (`Walk` in `crates/ascribe-resolve/src/fs.rs`), so each folder is walked once. It changes behavior, so it comes with a test (in `crates/ascribe-cli/tests/fmt.rs`, using `tests/support/links.rs`, since a conformance case can't hold a link) and a changelog line.

`design/tokens.toml` names a palette step by its lightness: 1000 × (1 − OKLCH L). `design/candidates/chosen.toml` names steps 50 to 975 instead. So the same color has two names, for example `indigo.435` and `indigo.600` for `#5962e8`. A test holds the shared colors equal, so a contributor who changes a shared color has to find the same hex under a different name in each file. `design/README.md` explains this for now (#179).

Choose one naming and use it in both files. Better still, generate one file from the other, since the assets and the specimen read `chosen.toml` and the stylesheets read `tokens.toml`.

Found in the agents pass (phase 11, #202; `project-docs/agents/pass-results.md`).

On a project with a few hundred warnings, `ascribe check --summary` shows which rules to work through, but nothing narrows `check` to one code. `--format concise` cuts at 50 lines, and its "and N more:" command narrows by file, not by rule. So an agent (or a person) can't fix one rule across the whole project from the concise output; it ends up working file by file.

Proposal to design: a `--code <code-or-slug>` filter on `ascribe check` (repeatable), applied after the check like the path filter, and the same argument on the MCP tool `ascribe_check`. When the concise list is cut, its "next" command would keep the filter. Open questions: whether `--summary` should suggest it, and how it interacts with `--format prompt`.

Found in the agents pass (phase 11, #202; `project-docs/agents/pass-results.md`).

`ascribe agents hook <agent> --event stop` holds an agent only while there are errors (agents decision 12, phase 9). A project whose CI runs `ascribe check --deny-warnings`, as Getting started suggests, can still have the agent finish with warnings, which then fail CI.

To design: how a project says its warnings count, so the stop hook holds on them too. Options: a setting in `ascribe.toml` (which `check` could also read), an option on the hook command that `agents sync --with-hook` writes, or leaving it as is. Worth deciding after the hand runs in `project-docs/agents/hand-checks.md` show whether agents leave warnings behind.

## What

`packages/cli/src/binary.ts:56` exports `nativeBinaryPath`, described as a "backwards-compatible name for resolveBinary". At version 0.2.0 there is no installed base to be compatible with, so the alias is redundant.

## Where

- `packages/cli/src/binary.ts:56` — the alias itself
- `packages/cli/src/index.ts:7` — re-exports it from the package
- `packages/cli/test/cli.test.ts:2,40,53` — the only consumers, its own tests

## Why remove it

The project is greenfield (0.x, `publish = false` workspace, first releases); nothing outside this repo can depend on the old name. `resolveBinary` already covers the use case, with an options object instead of two positional arguments.

## Notes

A sweep for legacy/migration code (legacy markers, fallbacks, shims, unused deps via `cargo machete`, unused workspace members) found no other candidates; the MCP `LEGACY` protocol versions and the retired `ASC039` slug are recorded decisions, not bloat. This alias was the only actionable item.

content.body:
## What happens

`ascribe report links` runs lychee and reads its JSON. lychee also reads the project's own `lychee.toml`, which the [report guide](https://ascribed-dev.com/guides/report/) tells people they can use. When that file has `cache = true`:

- **Every moved link (`link-external-moved`, ASC169) disappears from the second run on.** lychee's cache keeps an address, a status, and a time, and nothing about a redirect. A reused answer comes back as "OK (cached)" with no redirect listed, so Ascribe has nothing to report.
- **lychee writes `.lycheecache` into the project's root,** a file the project didn't ask Ascribe for and probably doesn't ignore.

## To reproduce

With lychee 0.24.2, in a folder holding `lychee.toml` with the one line `cache = true`, give lychee two addresses that redirect, using the arguments Ascribe uses:

```sh
printf 'https://vale.sh/docs/install\nhttps://agentskills.io\n' > u.txt
lychee --format json --verbose --no-progress - < u.txt   # first run
lychee --format json --verbose --no-progress - < u.txt   # second run
```

| Run | `redirects` | `cached` | Entries in `redirect_map` |
|---|---|---|---|
| First | 2 | 0 | 2 |
| Second | 0 | 2 | 0 |

`.lycheecache` then holds `https://vale.sh/docs/install,200,…`: the status, and no sign that it moved.

## Why

`crates/ascribe-check/src/links.rs` starts lychee with `--format json --verbose --no-progress -` and nothing about the cache, so the project's `lychee.toml` decides.

## Fix

Pass `--cache=false` to lychee. A flag on the command line overrides the setting in `lychee.toml` (checked: with it, the file's `cache = true` has no effect and no `.lycheecache` is written).

Also, in `docs/content/guides/report.md`, where it says lychee reads its own `lychee.toml`: say that Ascribe turns lychee's cache off, and why.

A test with the stand-in checker can't show this, since it's about lychee's own behavior. The scheduled Report workflow, or the test that runs a real lychee if there is one, is where to hold it.

## Related

The [cache proposal](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/proposals/cache.md) (not yet on `main` when this was filed) is for Ascribe keeping link results itself, in a form that keeps redirects. This issue is the bug that exists without it.

## What to do

`ascribe check` carries `ascribe link`'s closest targets as the diagnostic's fixes, marked `unsafe`, so the lightbulb, the JSON, and the MCP tools all offer them. And `closest` looks for the link's heading id on other pages, which finds a renamed page however far its new name is from the old.

For the broken link, `check`'s JSON has `"next":"choose"` and `"fixes":[]`. The lightbulb's menu had "one entry: "Prompt agent: fix this problem"". `ascribe link 'keys.md#rotate-keys' --from docs/install-agent.md` printed one line and no `Closest:`; `ascribe_link` answered `"closest":[]`. `api-keys.md` was in the same folder, with a heading whose id is `rotate-keys`. From the [surface audit](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/surface-audit/findings.md), findings 13, 26, 49.

## What to do

- A command names a page back as it was given, from the folder it was run in (finding 13). This changes a value in `ascribe link`'s JSON; the maintainer agreed to that on 10 October 2026, and the change adds its line to `project-docs/decisions.md`.
- `ascribe permalinks retire --to`, `--page`, and `--under` accept the path `ascribe check` prints (finding 26). This one is a bug on its own: the right path is refused with a message that says the page has no permalink. What's written into `ascribe.toml` stays from the content root.
- A prompt says once which folder its commands are for, and every path in it is from there (finding 49).

The `permalinks` group hasn't released, so its part is free now and costs a changelog entry after the next release.

**Size:** Small, in three parts.

## What the audit found

### Finding 13: One page, two names in one answer

**Evidence.** "`check` says `docs/install-agent.md:93:90`, and `link`, given `--from docs/install-agent.md`, answers "doesn't work from install-agent.md"." In the MCP session: `"file":"docs/install-agent.md"` from one tool, and `"from":"install-agent.md"` from the next, for `"from": "docs/install-agent.md"` given.

Seen since: the two names are deliberate in one place. `outline`'s JSON has both, and the reference says "`page` is the path from the content root, as links write it, and `file` is from the project root, as `ascribe check` reports it." So `link`'s `from` is a `page` under a name that doesn't say so, answering an input given as a `file`. `permalinks retire --to`, `--page`, and `--under` take the `page` form only (finding 26).

**Cost.** An agent that takes a path from one answer and gives it to the next command is using two bases without being told. Both work as input today, so nothing broke.

### Finding 26: `permalinks retire` names a page from the content root, where other commands take a path from the current folder

**Evidence.** `--page <PAGE>`: "Retire every permalink this page declares … by its path from the content root". Tried on 10 October 2026 in a copy of `examples/quill`, whose content root is `docs`, with a permalink on a heading of `docs/keys.md`, from the project's folder. `ascribe render docs/keys.md --build site` and `ascribe render keys.md --build site` both wrote the page. `ascribe permalinks retire --page keys.md --reason test` answered `retired rotate-keys`. `ascribe permalinks retire --page docs/keys.md --reason test` answered `` error: can't retire `docs/keys.md`: it declares no permalinks, and the list has none there ``, exit 2.

**Cost.** The path that every other command takes, and that `check` prints, is refused here with a message that says the page has no permalinks when it has one. Someone would go and look for a missing `permalink=true` that isn't missing.

### Finding 49: A prompt names its paths from the repository's root, to an agent standing in the project

**Evidence.** [Journey 7](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/surface-audit/journeys/edit-an-unfamiliar-project.md): the prompt ends "When you're done, run `ascribe check handbook/pages/security/content`". "From `handbook/pages/security`, where the agent ran the prompt: `error: handbook/pages/security/content doesn't exist`, exit 2. From the root it works." [Journey 5](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/surface-audit/journeys/review-a-pull-request.md): "The prompt names the pages from the project, `content/guides/rollouts.md`, and the project from the repository, `Project: docs/`", and from the root "`ascribe render content/guides/rollouts.md --build site --config docs` answers `` error: `content/guides/rollouts.md` isn't a page or fragment of the project ``."

**Cost.** A command copied out of a prompt works from one folder and fails from another, and the prompt doesn't say which. Both agents happened to be standing where it worked, or worked round it.

From the [surface audit](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/surface-audit/findings.md), findings 9, 10.

## What to do

- A *problem* is what Ascribe found in your project. A *diagnostic* is the kind of problem, with a code, that the reference and `ascribe explain` describe. Rename what departs; `ascribe report`'s "findings" become problems.
- `ascribe check --format prompt` counts as the summary line does: "Fix the 1 error", with advice listed after it as something to look at.

Before renaming anything in `ascribe report`: if its JSON has a `findings` key, the rename touches the commands' JSON and needs a decision first. Check, and stop if so.

**Size:** Small.

## What the audit found

### Finding 9: Five words for what Ascribe reports

**Evidence.** From the inventory: "The registry, `explain`, the JSON, and the plugin's server say *diagnostic*; the docs for `concise`, the Problems panel, the prompts, the MCP tool, and the skill say *problem*; `report` says *finding*; Vale's are *alerts*; the summary line and the hooks count *errors*, *warnings*, *advice*." One tool has both: `ascribe_explain` is titled "Explain a diagnostic", and `ascribe_check` reports "every *problem*".

**Cost.** Someone who reads "problem" in the editor and "diagnostic" in `--help` has to work out they're one thing. Nobody on the walks was stopped by it.

### Finding 10: What counts as a problem depends on who's told

**Evidence.** For one project: `Fix the 2 problems `ascribe check` reports in this project.`, and `checked 4 files: 1 error, 0 warnings, 1 advice`. The hook after an edit reports "*errors*, at most 10, errors only". The skill says "fix every *error*, and the *warnings* your edit caused".

**Cost.** An agent handed the prompt is told to fix advice that the hook and the skill tell it to leave alone.

From the [surface audit](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/surface-audit/findings.md), findings 14, 15, 19, 56, 62.

## What to do

Six small things, each a line of text output:

- `ascribe check` prints a diagnostic's help when it has no fix to name (14).
- Its last line names the builds it covered, or says "every build", prints all three counts every time, and has one form (15, 23).
- `ascribe link`'s `Write:` gives the empty form, `[](target)`, too (19).
- `ascribe render` says, above a switcher's arms, that a reader sees one of them and which dimension chooses (56).
- `ascribe diff` prints the commit once, and `ascribe explain` with no code says `--list` exists (62).
- The command reference states the exit codes of `agents rules`, `agents skill`, `agents prompt`, `agents hook`, and `sources status` (20).

The text output isn't a contract, so none of these needs a decision.

**Size:** Small, six times.

## What the audit found

### Finding 14: `check`'s text gives a next step only when there's a fix to apply

**Evidence.** For `ASC036` the text has the message and the source, and "No `Help:` line (an `ASC041` in the reference's sample has one, from its fix's title)". The JSON for the same diagnostic has `"help":"Fix the path, or create the file. Names must match exactly, including case, and the file must be inside the project."`

**Cost.** A person at a terminal gets less than a tool reading JSON, and has to know to run `ascribe explain`.

### Finding 15: `check`'s last line doesn't say which builds it covered

**Evidence.** After `checked 4 files: 0 errors, 0 warnings`, the agent with the plugin ran `for b in site cloud self-managed-3.3; do ascribe check --build $b 2>&1 | tail -1; done`, and reported "0 errors, 0 warnings, on the default check and on each of the `site`, `cloud` and `self-managed-3.3` builds." The JSON has `"builds_checked":["site","cloud","self-managed-3.3"]`.

Seen again in phase 3: an agent "checked one build's render and described three", with nothing in the line to prompt it ([journey 2](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/surface-audit/journeys/add-a-platform-section.md)). And the line has two forms: "`ascribe check content` ends `checked 6 files, reported on 6: 0 errors, 0 warnings`, and `ascribe check` ends `checked 6 files: 0 errors, 0 warnings`" ([journey 7](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/surface-audit/journeys/edit-an-unfamiliar-project.md)).

**Cost.** A careful agent checks three more times to learn what one word would have told it.
- **Seen again in phase 3:** an agent "checked one build's render and described three", with nothing in the line to prompt it ([journey 2](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/surface-audit/journeys/add-a-platform-section.md)). And the line has two forms: "`ascribe check content` ends `checked 6 files, reported on 6: 0 errors, 0 warnings`, and `ascribe check` ends `checked 6 files: 0 errors, 0 warnings`" ([journey 7](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/surface-audit/journeys/edit-an-unfamiliar-project.md)).

### Finding 19: `link` tells the walker to write more than the fix needs

**Evidence.** "`link` said `Write: [Rotate keys](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/surface-audit/api-keys.md#rotate-keys)`, and the page had `[](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/surface-audit/keys.md#rotate-keys)`, with no text. Wasn't sure whether to put the text in."

**Cost.** A moment's doubt, and a diff larger than the fix if it's followed.

### Finding 56: `ascribe render` can't show that readers see one arm of a switcher at a time

**Evidence.** [Journey 2](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/surface-audit/journeys/add-a-platform-section.md): "for a switcher it shows every arm in a row under a bold label: `**macOS**`, steps, `**Linux**`, steps, `**Windows**`, steps. The task's point, one system at a time, can't be seen in it. The agent said it was so without seeing it, and the preparer had to build and read `<ascribe-tabs sync="os">` in the `site` output to know."

**Cost.** The command the skill gives for "a page as one build's readers see it" shows a switcher the same as three sections in a row. An agent reports the difference on trust.

### Finding 62: Smaller things at the command line

**Evidence.** - "`ascribe diff --base 8254eaf` starts `compared with 8254eaf (8254eaf)`: the revision as given, then the commit, the same thing twice when a commit is given." (Journey 5.)
  - "`ascribe explain` with no code prints a usage error, and the agent's first search of it found nothing. `--list` was one `--help` away." (Journey 3.)
  - "To get the builds' names it ran `ascribe model --section builds --format json` and picked the names out with `grep -o '"name": *"[^"]*"'`". (Journey 4.)
  - "`refs` after the rename: `phrase:cloud doesn't exist.`, with exit 1. That's the answer the agent wanted, given as a failure." (Journey 4.)

**Cost.** Each is a moment.

From the [surface audit](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/surface-audit/findings.md), findings 46, 47, 59, 17.

## What to do

- Where a project's rules are when there's no `AGENTS.md`: `ascribe agents rules` prints them (46).
- A line each for `ascribe diff` and `ascribe drift` in the commands, how a source and a dimension are declared in the directive reference, and the two commands a CI job runs (47).
- The plugin's `new-page` command takes the request, tells the agent to read `ascribe model` for the type, then gives the prompt (59).
- The plugin's description says what each part is for: the skill for every agent, the tools for one with no shell, the hook for one that doesn't check (17).

The skill and the plugin are generated from the binary; edit the sources and bless.

**Size:** Small.

## What the audit found

### Finding 46: The skill sends an agent to two places that aren't there

**Evidence.** [Journey 3](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/surface-audit/journeys/show-an-example-from-code.md). The skill: "A project's own rules … are in the `AGENTS.md` beside its `ascribe.toml`". "The agent tried `AGENTS.md` and `docs/AGENTS.md` and got `Exit code 1`. That file is `ascribe agents sync`'s, and a project with the plugin alone has none." The directive reference: "Which note types, dimensions, and sources a project has: `ascribe model`." With a source declared, "`ascribe model` prints page types, dimensions, phrases, and builds, and no sources, and `ascribe model --section sources` answers `error: invalid value 'sources' for '--section <NAME>'`".

**Cost.** The agent's first two moves on a task about sources were dead ends the skill pointed it at.

### Finding 47: The skill doesn't say how to do five things the sessions needed

**Evidence.** - **Declare a source and mark a region.** "What taught the agent … was `ascribe explain` on diagnostics it hadn't been given: `ASC127`'s "declare one with `[sources.<name>]` and the `path` of the folder the code is in" and `ASC131`'s "mark one with `:snippet-start: {region}` and `:snippet-end:` comments". The skill's directive reference has one line on `@snippet`, and it doesn't say either." ([Journey 3](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/surface-audit/journeys/show-an-example-from-code.md).)
  - **Add a dimension.** "Adding a dimension isn't described anywhere the agent looked … The agent copied the shape of `[dimensions.deployment]` from the lines above". ([Journey 2](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/surface-audit/journeys/add-a-platform-section.md).)
  - **Show that a change changed nothing for readers.** "The agent built its own comparison: eighteen `ascribe render` calls into a scratch folder and `diff -r` … `ascribe diff` answers the same question in one command … The skill's list … has `explain`, `model`, `outline`, `link`, `render`, `refs`, and `check --summary`, and not `diff`." ([Journey 4](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/surface-audit/journeys/rename-a-phrase.md).)
  - **Know when an example changed.** "The agent never ran `ascribe drift`, the command for the task's second half, and the word isn't in the skill." (Journey 3.)
  - **Check in CI.** "Nothing the agent had says how to check a project in CI. Not the copy, not `ascribe --help`, not the skill: the word isn't in the skill." ([Journey 6](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/surface-audit/journeys/set-up-ci-checks.md).)

**Cost.** Each agent got there, by copying, by reading error messages, or by building its own tool. The skill is the one thing of the plugin's that agents used (finding 17), and it's silent on five of the seven tasks.

### Finding 59: The plugin's `new-page` command needs the answer before it can ask

**Evidence.** [Journey 7](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/surface-audit/journeys/edit-an-unfamiliar-project.md): "it's a wrapper round a command line: "Run `ascribe agents prompt new-page --arg type=<type> --arg title=<title> [--arg path=<path>]`". The agent couldn't run it until it knew the type, and to know the type it had to find the project and read its model, which is most of the job. The command's `argument-hint` is `<type> <title> [path]`, and the agent gave it the request's sentence." Of the three sessions: "The session with the most help took the most steps".

**Cost.** The one plugin command an agent reached for added steps to the task it was for.

### Finding 17: With a shell, an agent uses the plugin's skill, and nothing else of it

**Evidence.** Phase 1, two runs: `ascribe check`, `grep`, `cat`, and `git mv` in Bash, and neither "loaded the skill, called one of the plugin's tools, or used `LSP`." Phase 3, five sessions with the plugin, on harder tasks: four loaded the skill first and worked from it, and one ran the command `ascribe:new-page`. None called one of the plugin's tools or `LSP`: the notes say so of each ("The plugin's tools and commands weren't used", "never called one of the plugin's tools or `LSP`"). The stop hook ran in all seven and said nothing in each: `"stdout": ""`, `"exit_code": 0`. No diagnostic reached an agent after an edit: "Both edits were made by a script in the shell", and the one session that used `Write` and `Edit` got nothing back. In [journey 7](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/surface-audit/journeys/edit-an-unfamiliar-project.md), the same page was written with the plugin (25 seconds), with `ascribe agents sync`'s files (21), and with nothing (22): "The help changed the route, not the result or the time."

**Cost.** None to these agents. To the project, a plugin whose description promises "the language server's diagnostics after each edit" to an agent that edits through its shell and never gets them, and nine tools that an agent with a shell passes over for the commands they wrap.

From the review of #318 (non-blocking note), left out of #332.

## What happens

In a repository with several projects that install Ascribe differently (one pins `@ascribed/cli` in a `package.json`, another uses a global install, or two pin it in different `package.json` files), `ascribe agents sync --cloud` prints one MCP settings document per install, joined by a blank line (`crates/ascribe-cli/src/commands/agents.rs`, `mcp_settings.join("\n")`). Each is a whole `{"mcpServers": {"ascribe": …}}` document, and every one names its server `ascribe`, so the text can't be pasted into the repository's Copilot MCP settings as it stands, and merging them by hand collides on the server name.

## What done looks like

- `sync --cloud` prints one JSON document that can be pasted as it is.

content.body:
From the [cache proposal](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/097cc3d496fa2f3b08a69958ccacc50c76849126/project-docs/proposals/cache.md), its first half. The proposal has the design in full; this issue is what to build from it. The proposal's open questions are decided, below.

## What to do

`ascribe report links` doesn't ask again about an address that answered a few days ago.

- **A store of good answers,** `.ascribe/cache/links/`: one file an address, named by a hash of its key, written to a `tmp-` file and renamed. An entry says an address answered with nothing to report, on a day. A link that moved, failed, or timed out is never an entry, so **every finding in a report was asked about in that run.**
- **The key** is the address exactly as it's handed to lychee, and a hash of the project's `lychee.toml`. Not the redirect chain, and not lychee's version. Ascribe hashes the file and doesn't interpret it.
- **`[checks.links] reuse-days`,** 14 by default, and `0` asks about every address on every run. Each address's own limit falls between half of that and all of it, fixed by its hash, so addresses first checked together don't all come due on one day.
- **Days, not seconds.** The binary hands the libraries the day, as it does for `review-overdue`, so `ASCRIBE_TODAY` makes a test of expiry the same on any date.
- **`--recheck`** asks about every address and replaces the entries.
- **Cleanup needs no command:** a run deletes each entry too old to reuse, and a `tmp-` file over a day old.
- **A reader trusts nothing:** a file that doesn't parse, has another version, or holds a different address is treated as absent. A write that fails is skipped.
- **The report says what it did:** `Checked 1786 addresses: asked about 64, and reused 1722 answers, the oldest from 28 September.` A first run says nothing was remembered. The Markdown format says the same.
- **The JSON's `links` gains `asked`, `reused`, and `oldest_answer`,** and changes nothing: `checked` stays the sum, and `schema_version` stays 1.
- **In CI:** the docs' recipe and this repository's `.github/workflows/report.yml` restore and save the two folders with `actions/cache`, under a key that's new each run and restored by prefix, and both move from weekly to daily. With the cache a daily run asks about roughly a tenth of the addresses, and GitHub removes a cache nobody has read for seven days.

The proposal's "Several writers, and a crash" and "What never depends on it" are requirements, not background:

- These files aren't the project's sources, so they're read outside `ascribe_resolve::FileSystem`, with the comment that says why. `lychee.toml` is a project file and goes through it.
- A test holds that only the report's code opens `.ascribe/cache/`, as `file_reads.rs` holds file reads. `check`, `build`, `diff`, `drift`, `fmt`, the language server, and the hook never read or write it.

## The thread to prove first

The proposal's: the job on Ascribe's own docs runs twice, and the second run's summary says it asked about 1 address and reused 13. That's entries written by one process on one machine and trusted by another, through `actions/cache`. If it fails, the store's place or its key is wrong, and it's cheaper to learn that before the rest is built.

## Decided

The maintainer said yes to each on 11 October 2026.

- **The default is 14 days, and it's a setting from the start,** since `0` is the off switch and has to exist anyway (the proposal's question 2).
- **The recipe and `report.yml` go daily** (question 4).
- **A run doesn't ask twice** (question 3). Measured, a second pass cleared 5 of 77 failures and cost 20 seconds, and the history in the follow-up issue is the better answer to the same noise.

Each is a change to the content model or to a command's JSON, so the pull request adds them to `project-docs/decisions.md`. Nothing here waits on an answer.

## What else it touches

- `docs/content/reference/content-model.md` (`[checks.links]`), the command reference, `guides/report.md`, and `CHANGELOG.md`.
- The reference stops saying `.ascribe/` is written again whenever it's needed without saying what deleting it costs: time, and nothing else.
- The table of files Ascribe writes into a project (#283), and the map of the surface.
- lychee's own cache is already turned off (`--cache=false`, from #239), which this relies on.

**Size:** Medium.

content.body:
From the [cache proposal](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/097cc3d496fa2f3b08a69958ccacc50c76849126/project-docs/proposals/cache.md), its second half: "The history". Needs #339 first, which builds the store's place, the day, and the CI recipe this uses.

## What to do

`ascribe report links` reports a link as broken only when it has reason to believe it.

> A link that fails is reported, unless the history shows it answering before. Then it's **unconfirmed** until it has kept failing for `confirm-days`, with no answer in between.

- **`.ascribe/history/links.json`:** for each address, the last day it answered and the day it started failing, and whether the last run reported it. One file, sorted, written whole through a rename after each run. It forgets an address the pages no longer link to.
- **`[checks.links] confirm-days`,** 3 by default, and `0` reports every failure at once.
- **A failure that says the page is gone, a 404 or a 410, is reported at once.** Every other failure can be held.
- **A first run reports everything.** Holding takes evidence: a link is held only because this project's checker got an answer from that address before.
- **An unconfirmed link is shown, not hidden.** It has its own list, with its status and both dates. It isn't a problem: it's not counted, it doesn't make `--exit-code` fail, and it's left out of `--format prompt`.
- **An acknowledged link stays acknowledged,** and a moved link is never held: a permanent redirect is an answer, not a failure.
- **`--no-history`** reports as a first run would, and still records what it saw.
- **What's new:** the history knows what the last run reported, so the report says which problems are new since then and how many went away.
- **The JSON's `links` gains `previous_run`, `new`, `resolved`, and `unconfirmed`** (a capped list, as the others are), and changes nothing. `diagnostics` is untouched, and `schema_version` stays 1.

The proposal's "What the report says" has the text, word for word, for a run with both stores and for a first run.

## Decided

The maintainer said yes to each on 11 October 2026.

- **A 404 or a 410 is reported at once, and isn't held** (the proposal's question 1). The rule stays one sentence with one exception: a failure that says the page is gone isn't the kind that's back tomorrow. Of the thirteen 404s measured, one passed when asked again, which is the cost of this choice. Every other failure (a 5xx, a 429, a refusal, a timeout, a network error) is held.
- **The default is 3 days, and it's a setting from the start,** since `0` is the off switch.

Each is a change to the content model, to what a report says, or to a command's JSON, so the pull request adds them to `project-docs/decisions.md`. Nothing here waits on an answer.

## Requirements from the proposal

- When two runs finish together, one run's observations are lost. That can make a link's confirmation later and never earlier; a test shows it.
- Deleting the history costs one noisier report and never a missed finding. The reference says so plainly, since `.ascribe/` is a folder people delete.
- Only the report's code opens `.ascribe/history/`, held by the same test as the cache's.
- Tests are exact: a stand-in checker, a day from `ASCRIBE_TODAY`, and a store in a temporary folder give the same bytes every time. One test for each row of the proposal's table of what the history says.

## What else it touches

`docs/content/reference/content-model.md`, the command reference, `guides/report.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, the table of files Ascribe writes into a project (#283), and the map of the surface.

**Size:** Medium.

From the [surface audit](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/surface-audit/findings.md), finding 29, carved out of the [page templates plan](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/page-templates/README.md) ("Carved out, and waiting").

## What to do

A command of `@ascribed/astro`'s writes into an Astro project, once, the files every site built with Ascribe writes again: the content collection (`src/content.config.ts`), the route (`src/pages/[...slug].astro`), a layout that loads the elements, and the sidebar's list. From then on the files are the site's own, as `ascribe templates eject` leaves a project's templates. The Astro guide's steps 4 to 6 become that command.

It's the integration's, not the binary's: a different package and a different seam from the page templates plan, whose command is named `ascribe templates eject` so that a second thing to eject fits beside it.

**Waits on a design for navigation.** The sidebar's list is one of the four files, and what it holds depends on whether the content model ever gives a site its navigation (finding 28, which has no proposal; `site/README.md`'s "Navigation" says what it would take). Until that's decided, the starter can write the list as `site/src/nav.ts` has it today, kept complete by a test, and say so.

**Size:** Small for the starter itself.

## What the audit found

### Finding 29: Six more things the next site will write again

**Evidence.** Getting started ends its Astro steps with "Define the content collection, a route, and a layout that loads the elements. [Astro] walks through each file." `examples/astro-site/src` has the same `content.config.ts`, `pages/[...slug].astro`, `pages/404.astro`, and `layouts/Docs.astro` the site has. Of the rest: the search proposal says "Search for readers, and anything a site serves. That's Pagefind's job, or the site's choice."; the search and answers proposal says "What the host owns: status codes, headers, content negotiation, bot protection, logs.", and plans redirects while carving out "everything that needs to know what was published before". `site/public/_redirects` has no rule yet, and a 41-line test for the rules it will have. `links.test.ts` checks "Every link and anchor inside the built site", which no command of Ascribe's does for a site's own built pages.

**Cost.** A site builder copies four files from a guide before a page shows, then writes search, redirects, and a check of the built links themselves. Each is small; together they're 361 lines of this site.

**Recommendation.** Leave search, the table of contents, the not-found page, and the request for Markdown: each is decided, or already as small as it gets. Add a starter with the four files, so the guide's steps 4 to 6 are a command. Whether Ascribe checks a built site's own links, and notices a page whose address moved, is for the search and answers proposal's carved-out part, and should be said there.

Needs the compiler's half (#356) merged.

## What to build

In `@ascribed/astro`, from each project's `_ascribe/pages.json`:

- `@ascribed/astro/Head.astro`, given a page's entry: `<title>`, the description, the canonical link, and `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">` for `unlisted`. A `title` property is a function from the page's title and its record (with its route) to the whole title (decision 22). A page with no record gets nothing.
- One `sitemap.xml` at the site's root, absolute addresses, no dates: every listed page of every project with routes, and every other page Astro built, minus permalink forwarding pages, the not-found page, and a list of routes the site passes. No `site`, no sitemap, and a build warning saying why.
- One `robots.txt` at the root: a `User-agent: *` group with each project's lines, then the groups projects wrote whole, then the sitemap's address. Nothing at all when there'd be nothing in it. A site with its own `robots.txt` in `public/` keeps it, and the build says so. A site whose Astro `base` isn't `/` gets the sitemap under the base, no `robots.txt`, and a message with the lines the host's own file needs (decision 30).
- Both served in `astro dev` and written by `astro build`.

**This is the seam.** If the head can't be one component a layout includes, or the two files can't be written at the root for several projects in both commands, stop and report before going on.

## Done when

- Unit tests, and end-to-end tests in `examples/astro-site`, in a build and under `astro dev`: an `unlisted` page has `noindex`, isn't in `sitemap.xml` or `llms.txt`, and a page beside it with nothing set is in both; a project under a base path, whose lines come out with the base before them; two projects; a page of the site's own, in the sitemap; a site with its own `robots.txt`; a site with no `site`; a site whose `base` isn't `/`.

content.body:
A page of the site, `/credits/`, that says who builds Ascribe, what it's built on, and where its ideas came from. Each is said somewhere in the repository today, and none of it in one place a visitor would find.

## What to do

One Ascribe page in `site/home/content/`, like the landing page and "Why Ascribe", in three parts.

### Who builds Ascribe

"Built by Kyle Rollins with Claude": Kyle Rollins, with Claude, Anthropic's model, working through Claude Code. A sentence on how the work is divided: the maintainer decides what's built and reads what ships, and most of the code, the tests, and the docs are written by Claude under those decisions.

It names Claude and not one model, so the page doesn't need editing when the next one arrives.

### What Ascribe is built on

Grouped by what a reader would want to know. Each is a name, a link, and a few words on what Ascribe uses it for. No versions.

- **Inside the binary.** comrak first, with a paragraph of its own: Ascribe's parser is a fork of it, at a named release, with a link to the list of changes (`crates/comrak-ascribe/FORK.md`). Then the libraries that do visible work: clap, ariadne, serde, toml, and schemars.
- **In the npm packages.** Astro, and the libraries its Markdown goes through.
- **Programs Ascribe runs and doesn't ship.** Vale, lychee, and the delivery spec's checker, with what each is for.
- **Building Ascribe and its site.** Pagefind, Playwright, Vitest, and the rest of what a contributor meets.

### Where its ideas came from

| From | What Ascribe took |
|---|---|
| CommonMark | The language everything else is added to |
| Bluehawk | The snippet tags, kept as they are, so code already tagged for it works |
| AsciiDoc | A title on its own line |
| Swift's `@available` | Lifecycle states named by the version they start at |
| HTML's custom elements | A hyphen marks a project's own widgets |
| Elastic's docs-builder | Empty-text links filled from their target, and a large corpus to measure choices against |
| Ruby and Lua | A bare `@end` |
| The Web Documentation Delivery Spec | What a build publishes for AI agents |
| The Good Docs Project | The page templates, once they're built |
| Steel threads, by Jade Rubick | How every plan's phases are ordered |

Each row has a sentence on what was taken and a link to where Ascribe says so (`SPEC.md`'s Appendix C and D, the drift guide, the report guide). What the spec's rationale says Ascribe decided against (MDX, colon-fenced directives, GitHub's alerts) isn't a credit and stays in the spec.

## Keeping it true

- **"Ascribe uses this."** A new test compares the page with the manifests: every project the page names as a dependency is one, in `Cargo.toml` or a `package.json`, so a named dependency that's removed fails the test until the page follows. The reverse isn't required.
- **comrak's release** is read from `FORK.md`, not typed again.
- **"Ascribe took this from there."** The site's link test follows each row's link. A row with nowhere to link gets its sentence added to the docs first, not to `SPEC.md`: the spec changes only by a recorded decision, and this isn't one.
- **"This is who builds it."** Nothing can test it. The maintainer reads the page before it merges.

## What else it touches

- The page's social card, and the two tests that list the site's own pages (`site/test/e2e.test.ts`, `scripts/design/assets.test.ts`).
- The Credits link in the footer (#379). If the footer hasn't landed, the page ships without a way in and the footer's pull request adds it.
- The landing page's line about status ("early, and open source") could link here too.

**Size:** Small. No change to Ascribe itself.

## Decided

- The page is called "Credits", at `/credits/`.
- The wording is "Built by Kyle Rollins with Claude".
- The ideas table is the one above; what the repository already states is enough for now.

## Left out

- Every dependency: a full list is what a license report is for.
- License texts, and versions.
- A list of contributors. When there are more than two, the page points at the repository's own list.
- Thanks to people: projects and ideas only.

From the [proposal](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/b0d183ec/project-docs/proposals/credits-page.md).

Every pull request that records a decision appends to `project-docs/decisions.md` at the same place and claims the next number, so two of them conflict: on the lines, and on the number. Three commits touched the file on `main` within an hour on 11 October, one of them a merge of `main` into a branch, and #375 moved its decision into a plan to get out of a conflict.

The changelog had the same problem and #354 fixed it with a file per entry in `changes/`. A decision needs one thing more than a changelog entry: an id that's unique without two branches agreeing on it, because decisions are cited by number from about 30 files outside `project-docs/`.

## What to do

A new decision is a file of its own, identified by the number of the issue it was made for.

- **Where:** `project-docs/decisions/<number>-<slug>.md`, such as `project-docs/decisions/381-decision-files.md`. The number is the issue's. A decision with no issue uses its pull request's number. GitHub numbers issues and pull requests in one sequence, so two branches can't take the same one.
- **How it's cited:** "decision #381", with a link to the file where a link fits. An issue that produces more than one decision adds a letter: `381a-…`, `381b-…`, cited as "decision #381a".
- **What a file holds:** what an entry holds today, the decision in a bold sentence, then _Why:_ and _From:_, and the section it belongs to (The binary, Review, The language, and so on) as frontmatter.
- **The existing decisions stay where they are.** Decisions 1 to 123 keep their numbers and their place in `decisions.md`; nothing is renumbered and no citation changes. `decisions.md` takes no new numbered entries after this lands, and says so at its top.
- **A decision that's replaced** stays, as now: its file (or its struck-through entry in `decisions.md`) gains a pointer to the one that replaced it. A file isn't deleted and its number isn't reused.
- **One view of everything:** reading "every decision about the language" must still work. Either `decisions.md` gains a generated index of the files under each section, rewritten with `ASCRIBE_BLESS=1` like the other generated files, or a test holds a hand-kept index to the folder. The generated one must not bring the conflict back: an index every pull request rewrites is the same problem. If it can't be generated without that, a `README.md` in the folder that explains the layout, with the sections read from the files by a script on demand, is enough.
- **A test** (beside `scripts/release/changes.test.ts`, or in `scripts/repo-docs/`) checks each file: its name, its frontmatter's section is one of the known ones, it has the decision, a _Why:_ and a _From:_, and its links lead to files in the repository.
- **A `README.md` in the folder,** as `changes/README.md` is for the changelog: how to name a file, what to write, and how it's checked.

## What else changes

- `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`: "a decision … is added to `project-docs/decisions.md`" becomes the folder. CONTRIBUTING's note that a change to `decisions.md` runs the tests, not only the formatter, covers the folder too, and so does the path filter in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` that it describes.
- `project-docs/decisions.md`'s opening paragraphs: where a new decision goes, and that a plan's decisions which still bind when it closes move to files in the folder.
- The skills that say where a decision is recorded (`.claude/skills/`), and `project-docs/checklists.md` where it names the file.
- `scripts/repo-docs/paths.test.ts`, if it needs to know the folder.

## Not changing

- **A plan's own decisions.** They stay in the plan's `README.md` while it runs, numbered within the plan.
- **The 123 existing decisions,** and every citation of them.

**Size:** Small to medium. No change to Ascribe itself.

## Decided

- New decisions are identified by issue or pull request number, not the next number in a row. The other two ways were considered and turned down: files named by the next number (two branches can both take it, and nothing notices until the second runs CI again), and unnumbered files numbered when gathered (a pull request couldn't cite its own decision, and something would have to commit to `main` after every merge).

This issue's own decision is the first one recorded the new way.

The changelog page is too long to use, and the next release will make it worse. At 1280 wide it is 34 screens, and the unreleased section alone is 93 entries and about 26 of them, in one flat list. What makes it hard: - **Nothing to navigate by.** Four headings (Unreleased and three releases), no contents list, and no subheadings in Unreleased, though 0.2.0's 12 entries have seven. - **Entries are paragraphs.** The median is 65 words and the longest 349; only the bold first sentence can be scanned. - **The order is arbitrary.** Entries from `changes/` are gathered by file name. - **Everything has one weight.** A behavior change looks like a docs page that moved. ## The mockup Built from the real page, all 149 entries, with the site's own styles. It takes the page from 34 screens to about 12, and Unreleased from 26 to about 6. ## What to do In `site/src/pages/changelog.astro` and `site/src/changelog.ts`, which already rewrite the rendered HTML (`pointLinks`, `anchorReleases`): 1. **Collapse each entry to its bold sentence.** Each entry becomes a `
` whose `` is the bold sentence and whose body is the rest. No JavaScript is needed for that. "Expand all" and "Collapse all" buttons above the list. 2. **Group a release's entries by area,** under a heading with a count: the language and the content model, the `ascribe` command, the editor, Astro and the elements, agents, review, the docs and the site, and fixes. Released sections already have such headings; the page keeps them. 3. **A contents list beside the page:** each release, with its areas under the newest ones. The docs layout has one to borrow. Below the width where it fits, it goes above the list or behind a button; the mockup just hides it, which isn't enough. 4. **Badge behavior changes,** which already say "Behavior change:" in the bold sentence, and offer "Behavior changes only". For 2 to work, an entry has to say its area: - **Each file in `changes/` declares its area,** `scripts/release/changes.ts`'s gather writes it under that area's `###` heading in the unreleased section, and `changes.test.ts` checks the area is a known one. `changes/README.md` says how. - **The entries already in `CHANGELOG.md`'s unreleased section** (79 of them, flat) are sorted under the headings once, by hand, with no entry's words changed. ## What the mockup showed that collapsing doesn't fix - **A third of the bold sentences are long.** 49 of 149 run past two lines collapsed. A limit on the bold sentence's length would be a writing rule, held by `changes.test.ts` for new entries. - **14 unreleased entries have "Fixed:" as their bold text,** and would all collapse to "Fixed". The mockup puts them in a Fixes group and uses each one's first sentence as its summary. The real thing needs that as a stated convention, or those entries get a bold sentence. - **The command group is 26 entries.** Grouping finds the group; it doesn't shrink it. ## To decide in the pull request, each recorded as a decision - **How an entry declares its area.** A folder per area (`changes/editor/check-fix.md`) keeps the files as they are, plain list items; frontmatter changes what every entry file looks like. Recommended: the folder. - **Whether the bold sentence gets a length limit,** and what it is. - **What a "Fixed:" entry's summary is.** ## Constraints - **`CHANGELOG.md` stays one file, in the form it has.** It's what GitHub and a release show; the page is a rendering of it. Its `###` headings are the only change to it. - **Every `#v0.2.0`-style anchor keeps working,** and a link to an entry inside a closed `
` opens it. - **Finding text in the page still works.** A browser's find-in-page doesn't open a closed `
` everywhere; `hidden="until-found"` or opening everything when a search is likely needs checking in Chrome, Firefox, and Safari. - **Styles come from the design tokens,** and the page works at phone width without a horizontal scroll. - **A bad link still fails the build,** as now. ## Not in this issue - **A page per release.** It breaks the one-file model and every anchor; hold it until this proves not enough. - **Dropping or folding docs-only entries.** About a quarter of the unreleased entries are a guide added or a page moved. Whether those belong in the changelog is its own decision. **Size:** Medium. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Part of [the page templates plan](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/page-templates/README.md), [phase 2](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/page-templates/phase-2-thread.md), task 1. The first half of the steel thread's seam: their Markdown becoming a page Ascribe accepts, mechanically.

## What to build

- **The pin:** their tag `v1.6.0` and its commit at `gitlab.com/tgdp/templates` (README decision 25), in one file that the script and the test both read (decision 19).
- **A script under `scripts/`,** laid out like `scripts/surface/`, that fetches that commit's files into a folder git ignores and writes the how-to's template and guide by the steps in the phase's "The conversion": the block quotes about the template removed (decision 22); the level-1 heading moved into `title`, with a `description` placeholder from the rule file (decision 21); every opening `{` in the body escaped, except inside code (decisions 4, 17); the "See also" placeholder that runs across blocks left as their text has it (decision 20); the structural rules from a data file beside the script, each naming its template and the text it applies at (for the how-to, likely `@steps` on the procedure); instructions inside a section left as they are (decision 18); and `ascribe fmt`'s canonical form last. The template carries no line about where it came from (decision 23); the guide opens with one saying it's generated, from their repository, at which tag, under which license.
- **The committed copies,** in the crate that will carry them into the binary, with a generated file beside them listing each copy, their tag, and their index's summary of the type. **Default picked,** since the plan leaves the crate open: a new library crate, `crates/ascribe-templates`, which the later issues add `list`, `eject`, and `status` to. ARCHITECTURE.md says what it owns and lists the copies among the generated files.

If the how-to can't be made valid by steps like these, with no step that's "then fix it by hand", stop and report here.

## Done when

- A test regenerates the copies from the pinned tag and fails on a difference; `ASCRIBE_BLESS=1` rewrites them. Without network it's skipped and says so; it runs in CI.
- A test with no network: the committed template passes `ascribe check` in a project that declares its type (by hand in the fixture, since `template` doesn't exist yet) and `ascribe fmt` leaves it unchanged. Its body has no level-1 heading and no block quote about the template.
- The script's own tests: a brace inside a code span and a fenced block isn't escaped; a rule that doesn't find its place stops the script, naming the template and the place.

Split from the docs report in #423. The delivery spec's checks on `https://ascribed-dev.com/docs/` report two findings about what Ascribe's site writes:

- **[ASC170] `content-start-position` warns:** 23 of 50 sampled pages have their content starting 10–50% into the HTML (the worst at 36%). The navigation comes before the content.
- **[ASC171] `markdown-content-parity` fails:** 2 of 50 pages have substantive differences between their Markdown and HTML (on average 2% missing). The report says Ascribe's output should pass this check.

## What to do

1. **Parity first, since it's a failure.** Find the two pages the checker flags (`ascribe report agents --site` names them), work out what's missing from which side, and fix it where Ascribe writes it. This is probably a bug in Markdown or HTML output, and a fix comes with a conformance case. If the cause is in the Astro plugin, `tests/render/` and both renderers have to agree.
2. **Content position.** Put each page's main content earlier in the HTML than the navigation (for example, the sidebar after `<main>` in source order, and placed by CSS), or make sure the checker reads `<main>`. Find out which one the checker credits before choosing. This changes the site output's markup, so go through `project-docs/checklists.md` for that, and the `tests/render/` fixtures change. Keyboard order and screen readers must still work: a skip link, and a focus order that makes sense.

If the two parts turn out to be unrelated, it's fine to open two pull requests.

- The report's next run shows `markdown-content-parity` passing and `content-start-position` with no warning, or the PR says which pages still warn and why.

content.body:
Part of [the page templates plan](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/page-templates/README.md), found by [phase 7](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/page-templates/phase-7-docs.md) in #414: what a command would have to do to take a template for a type a project already declares, in one step.

## What happened

Ascribe's docs declared `reference` already, for `reference/**` and `contracts/**`, with `title` drawn as code (`inline = "code"`) and `description` marked `role = "description"`. Taking the set's reference took three steps:

1. `ascribe templates eject reference` refused, as decision 16 says, and wrote nothing:

   ```text
   Error: reference: ascribe.toml declares [types.reference] already
   wrote nothing
   ```

2. With `[types.reference]` taken out of `docs/ascribe.toml` by hand, eject wrote the template, its guide, Ascribe's notes, and `templates.lock`, and appended a new `[types.reference]` at the end of the file: `files = ["reference/**"]`, `template`, `guide`, and `title = "string"` and `description = "string"`.
3. By hand: the type moved back beside the docs' `guide` type, `contracts/**` put back in `files`, and `inline = "code"` and `role = "description"` put back on the fields. Only `template` and `guide` were kept from what eject added.

Between steps 1 and 3 the project was broken, and nothing said so: `ascribe check docs` was clean at each step. The contracts had fallen to the default type, and every reference page's title would have shown its backticks as text, since `title` was a plain string. A project that takes the set late is the only kind that has pages, so it's the one where that matters.

## What a command would have to do

Take a template for a type that exists and leave the type's own keys alone:

- **Write the files as eject does,** the template, its guide, and Ascribe's notes, refusing a file in the way, and record them in `templates.lock`.
- **Add only `template` and `guide`** to the existing `[types.<name>]`, in place, keeping its `files`, its frontmatter, its other keys, and every comment. That's an edit inside a table eject didn't write, which decision 28 avoids by only ever appending; it needs the same guarantee, that the result loads with the type in it or nothing is written. A type declared as an inline table, or one with `template` or `guide` already, is refused and named.
- **Check the type's frontmatter against the template's,** since the type keeps its own: a field the template's frontmatter has that the type doesn't declare, or declares with another type, would make every page started from the template fail. Refuse it and name the field, or say so, before writing.
- **Say what it left alone,** in the text and the JSON, as eject says what it added.

Whether that's a flag on `eject` (such as `--keep-type`, or `--existing`) or another verb is the decision this issue needs. Decision 16's refusal could then name it: "declares [types.reference] already; `<command>` takes the template for it".

## Done when

- One command takes a template for a declared type, writing the files and the two keys and nothing else in `ascribe.toml`, and `docs/ascribe.toml`'s reference is what it would have written, apart from `purpose`.
- Eject's refusal of a declared type names that command.
- The decision is recorded in `project-docs/page-templates/README.md` or `project-docs/decisions/`.

Part of [the page templates plan](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/page-templates/README.md), found by [phase 7](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/page-templates/phase-7-docs.md) in #415.

## What happened

After Ascribe's docs took the how-to, tutorial, and concept types, `ascribe check docs` reported two placeholders that the pages don't have:

```text
[ASC195] Advice: this page still has its template's placeholder `{product}`; write what it asks for in its place
    ╭─[ content/getting-started.md:77:3 ]
 77 │ - `{product}` and `{version}` are phrases from `ascribe.toml`.
```

```text
[ASC195] Advice: this page still has its template's placeholder `{Task name }`; write what it asks for in its place
    ╭─[ content/guides/templates.md:85:153 ]
 85 │ ... or with the space before its closing brace taken out, as the how-to's `\{Task name }` has, isn't the template's any more ...
```

The first is worse than it looks. A phrase named `product` is reported on a page of the tutorial type wherever it's used, in prose too, since the tutorial template's Background has `\{product}` as a placeholder. In a project from `ascribe init --templates` with `product` and `version` in `[phrases]`, this page gets the advice twice:

```markdown
---
title: Learn
description: Learn it.
---

You need {product} {version} or later.

Quote `{product}` here.
```

That's the sentence Ascribe's own notes on the tutorial tell a writer to write ("Versions are phrases. Write `You need {product} {version} or later`").

The second is a page about templates quoting a placeholder in inline code. #415 reworded both of the docs' sentences rather than acknowledging them.

## What to change

- **A phrase isn't a placeholder.** The template's placeholder is written `\{product}`, escaped, so it shows as text; a page's `{product}` is a phrase, and isn't the template's text. Compare what the page shows, or match only the escaped form.
- **Text in code isn't the page's own words.** Skip inline code and code blocks, where a page writes text as it is. The conversion never puts a template's placeholder in code.

## Done when

- A phrase with a placeholder's name, and a placeholder quoted in inline code or a code block, aren't reported; an untouched `\{product}` in a paragraph, a list item, or a heading still is.
- A conformance case shows each.
- The diagnostic's entry in `tests/conformance/diagnostics.toml` says so, and the templates guide's "What's left to fill in" if it needs it.

Part of [the page templates plan](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/page-templates/README.md), found by [phase 7](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/page-templates/phase-7-docs.md) in #415. #436 is the other half: a type the project declares already.

## What happened

Ascribe's docs took four types they didn't declare, in one step:

```text
$ ascribe templates eject how-to tutorial concept troubleshooting
...
added [types.how-to] to ascribe.toml, for pages under content/how-to/
added [types.tutorial] to ascribe.toml, for pages under content/tutorial/
added [types.concept] to ascribe.toml, for pages under content/concept/
added [types.troubleshooting] to ascribe.toml, for pages under content/troubleshooting/
```

Then every key it wrote but `template` and `guide` was rewritten by hand:

- **`files`.** The docs' 14 pages for those types are under `guides/`, plus `getting-started.md`, so each type's `files` became a list of the pages it holds. Until then, each type matched no page, every page stayed of the default type, and `ascribe check docs` was clean: nothing said four types had no pages.
- **The frontmatter.** Eject wrote `title = "string"` and `description = "string"` on each. The docs' types all have `title = { type = "string", inline = "code" }` and `description = { type = "string", role = "description" }`, so the same two lines went on four types by hand. Without them, the site would have shown backticks in those pages' titles.

A project that takes the set late is the one that has pages, and its pages aren't in folders named for the set's types.

## What a command could do

Two things, either of which would have saved the hand edits:

- **Say when a type it added matches no page,** with the pages that are of the default type, so the writer knows `files` is theirs to change. The check could say it too, as advice on a type with `files` that match nothing.
- **Take the project's frontmatter for the new types,** when the project has a default type: copy its `title` and `description` declarations rather than writing plain strings, as long as they're still strings the template's frontmatter fits.

A `--files` option, naming each type's pages at eject, is the third, and probably too much for one command line.

## Done when

- Eject in a project with pages says, for a type it added, that it matches no page yet.
- The decision on the frontmatter is recorded in `project-docs/page-templates/README.md` or `project-docs/decisions/`, and done if it's yes.

## What happened

**Troubleshooting: the template's headings warn.** The template has a `###` heading for each cause and its solution under each symptom (`Cause 1 of symptom 1`, `Solution or workaround to cause 1 of symptom 1`). Filled in the obvious way, with "Cause" and "Solution" under each symptom, the review guide's troubleshooting page got 14 warnings:

```text
[ASC046] Warning: this heading's text gives the same slug as another heading on the page, so its id is numbered and can change when headings move; give it a stable id with `@id`
    ╭─[ content/guides/review/troubleshooting.md:28:1 ]
 28 │ ### Cause
```

The docs wrote them as bold paragraphs, `**Cause.**` and `**Solution.**`, instead. `troubleshooting.ascribe.md` says nothing about it, though it's the first thing a writer meets.

**How-to and tutorial: steps that are headings.** The notes on both say the steps are one `@steps` list. Three of the docs' pages, getting started, content that varies, and the Astro guide's set-up, number their steps as headings (`## 1. Declare a dimension`, `### 1. Install`), since each step holds a file, a command, and its output, which a list item holds badly. The table in [docs-types.md](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/page-templates/docs-types.md) kept them as headings. The notes don't say when that's the better shape, or that `@steps` doesn't apply to it.

## What to change

- `troubleshooting.ascribe.md`: a line saying to write each cause and solution as a bold paragraph, or to give each heading an `@id`, since `heading-duplicate-without-id` warns about the same heading under every symptom.
- `how-to.ascribe.md` and `tutorial.ascribe.md`: a line saying that a step holding a file and its output can be a heading of its own, numbered, with no `@steps`.

The notes are copied into a project by `eject` and recorded in `templates.lock`, so the docs' copies in `docs/templates/` change with them.

content.body:
A page says what type it is, in its frontmatter. Today a type applies to a page by where its file is, and that forces a project to give each type a folder.

## Why

A project's folders should be its features, with every type of page about a feature in one folder: review's tutorial, how-to, reference, and troubleshooting together. A reader shouldn't go to another part of the site for related content, and a sidebar grouped by content type ships the docs' own filing system to people who don't care about it.

Types work against that today:

- **A type applies by path.** `[types.<name>] files` is a list of patterns, and `default = true` takes the rest. A how-to and a reference page in one folder can only be told apart by naming files one by one, which `docs/ascribe.toml` does: eight paths under `[types.how-to]`.
- **The starter set gives each type a folder.** `ascribe templates eject` writes `files = ["how-to/**"]`, so a new project's folders are its types from its first day.

## Decided

By the maintainer, 12 October 2026. Record these as a file in `project-docs/decisions/`, numbered by this issue, in the pull request.

1. **Every page declares its type in its frontmatter, with the reserved key `type`.** Its value is the name of a type `ascribe.toml` declares.
2. **`files` and `default` are removed from `[types.<name>]`.** There's one way to say a page's type. Ascribe is before 1.0 with no users, so there's no period where both work and no migration command: a project that still has either key gets the unknown-key error, with a message that names `type:`.
3. **A project that declares no types needs nothing.** Its pages have no type, as now.
4. **The starter set stops giving each type a folder.** A template carries its type in its frontmatter, so a page made from one is typed from its first line, wherever it's saved.

## What to do

### The language

- `type` is a reserved frontmatter key for pages (SPEC §2.1), beside `available`, `variant`, `permalink`, `listing`, and `intended`. A fragment can't use it (`frontmatter-reserved-in-fragment`), and a type can't declare a field with that name (`model-field-reserved`).
- In a project that declares types:
  - a page with no `type` is an error at the page, with a fix for each declared type (next step `choose`);
  - a `type` that isn't declared is an error at the value, with the closest name as a fix.
- `content-type-unresolved` (a page matched by more than one type, or by none with no default) can't happen any more. Its code isn't reused: the diagnostics file keeps the entry as no longer reported, as it does for others that were retired, or the new errors take its place if that's the cleaner reading of the contract. Say which in the pull request.
- `model.type_for(path)` has 13 callers, in `ascribe-check`, `ascribe-lsp`, `ascribe-query`, `ascribe-resolve`, `ascribe-templates`, and `ascribe-model` itself (`[listing.types]`). A page's type now needs its frontmatter, so the type is resolved once, in the source index, and read from there. Find out first whether every caller has the index: the `[listing]` rules in `ascribe-model` take a path today.
- The generated Zod schema is a `z.union` of the types' schemas. With `type` in every page it can be a discriminated union on `type`. That's a change to a generated file a site imports, so name it in the changelog entry.
- `ascribe fmt`: where `type` goes in canonical frontmatter order.

### Everything that showed or used `files`

- `ascribe model`, in text and JSON: a type no longer has `files`. The JSON is a contract; its schema changes with a recorded decision (this one).
- The rules `ascribe agents sync` writes: each type's line says what it's for and its frontmatter, and no longer where its pages go.
- `ascribe agents prompt new-page`, the plugin's `/ascribe:new-page`, and the editor's **Ascribe: New Page**: each said or decided where a type's file goes from `files`. Now the page goes where the person or the request says, and gets `type:` written in it.
- `ascribe report`'s inventory by type, the editor's Pages view, `ascribe outline`: unchanged in what they show, and now reading the declared type.
- `[listing.types]` is unchanged: a rule for every page of a type.

### The starter set

- Each converted template's frontmatter gains `type: <name>`. The conversion script writes it, and the copies are regenerated; nobody edits one by hand.
- `ascribe templates eject` adds each type with `template`, `guide`, `purpose` or its summary, and its frontmatter, and no `files`. Its message no longer says a type "matches no page".
- `--keep-type` stays: it takes a template for a type the project declares already.
- `ascribe init --templates` follows.
- `template-placeholder-left` and the other checks that compare a page with its type's template read the declared type.
- The page templates plan (`project-docs/page-templates/README.md`) says `files = ["<name>/**"]` in its decision 16. Amend it there, pointing at this issue's decision.

### The projects in this repository

- `docs/`, `site/home`, `site/demo`, and every project under `examples/` that declares types: add `type:` to each page and remove `files` and `default`. In `docs/` that's 48 pages, each getting the type `docs/ascribe.toml` gives it today, so no page's type changes.
- The conformance cases: about 60 have an `ascribe.toml` that declares types. Each page in them gains `type:`. New cases for the two errors, and for a project with no types.
- This issue doesn't move any docs page. Regrouping Ascribe's docs by feature is separate work that follows this.

### The docs

- SPEC §2.1 and §7.2, and the appendix's example.
- `docs/content/reference/content-model/` and its contract: `[types.<name>]` loses two keys.
- The directive reference's frontmatter section, getting started, the templates guide, and the agents guide.
- An entry in `changes/` that says **Behavior change**.

## Checks

- Go through "A change to the language" in `project-docs/checklists.md` first.
- `node scripts/compare/outputs.ts --base main`: the site, plain, and JSON outputs of every project should be the same except where frontmatter is shown (the JSON output's frontmatter, and the Zod schema). Name each accepted file.
- `node scripts/surface/inventory.ts`, and read its diff.

**Size:** Large. One pull request for the language change and the repository's own projects, since neither builds without the other. The starter set's change can be a second commit in it, or a second pull request straight after.

## Not in this issue

- Navigation. The [proposal](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/proposals/navigation.md) takes a section to be a folder and orders a section's pages by type; it reads the type this issue gives a page.
- Moving Ascribe's docs into folders by feature.
- A command that adds `type:` to a project's pages. The fix on each page does it, and `ascribe check --fix` can't choose a type for a page.

Renaming a page a glossary term links to leaves the term's `link` pointing at the old path. The project then has a model error, and every later `ascribe rename` refuses.

## To reproduce

In a copy of `examples/monorepo`, whose glossary terms link to `reference/glossary.md`:

```console
$ cd docs
$ ascribe rename reference/glossary.md reference/terms.md
changed content/index.md (1 place)
moved content/reference/glossary.md to content/reference/terms.md
$ grep glossary.md ascribe.toml
link = "/reference/glossary.md#feature-flag"
link = "/reference/glossary.md#rollout"
link = "/reference/glossary.md#segment"
$ ascribe check
… model-glossary-link, three times
$ ascribe rename getting-started.md renamed-page.md
error: ascribe.toml has errors; `ascribe check` lists them
```

Reproduced on `main` at `46ec166b`, with a debug build.

## What should happen

The rename changes each glossary term's `link` to the page's new path, keeping its `#id`, and reports `ascribe.toml` among the files it changed, as it does for a page. `ascribe.toml` is edited in place, keeping its comments and order, as `ascribe permalinks retire` edits it.

The command's help says it changes "everything that uses it, as the editor's rename does". Check whether the editor's rename has the same gap; if it does, fix both, since they're meant to be one behavior.

## Also check

Anything else in `ascribe.toml` that names a page or a folder by path and should follow a move: `[listing.folders]`, when a folder's last page leaves it or a folder is renamed, and any other key that holds a path into the content root. Say in the pull request which were checked and which follow.

## How it was found

Moving 32 of Ascribe's own docs pages for #452. Each glossary link had to be fixed by hand between renames.

`ascribe rename` with `--config <dir>` fails when it's run from outside the project, though its help says a path is "from the current directory, or from the content root".

## To reproduce

In a copy of `examples/monorepo`, from the folder above the project:

```console
$ ascribe rename reference/glossary.md reference/terms.md --config docs
error: The project has no pages to rename in.
$ echo $?
2
$ cd docs && ascribe rename reference/glossary.md reference/terms.md
changed content/index.md (1 place)
moved content/reference/glossary.md to content/reference/terms.md
```

The same from Ascribe's own repository root with `--config docs`. Reproduced on `main` at `46ec166b`, with a debug build.

## What should happen

With `--config`, the command finds the project it names, reads TARGET and NEW from the current directory or from that project's content root, as its help says, and renames. Every other command that takes `--config` works from the repository's root (`ascribe check --config docs`, `ascribe build --config docs`), and CI and agents run them that way.

The message is also wrong for what happened: the project has pages. If a path can't be found, the error should name the path and the two places it was looked for.

## Worth checking with it

Whether the other targets (`phrase:<key>`, `value:<value>`, a heading's id) work from outside the project with `--config`, and a test for each from the folder above.

## How it was found

Moving Ascribe's own docs pages for #452, from the repository's root.

One docs page has a Markdown link in its frontmatter `description`, where it's plain text and never a link.

`docs/content/contracts/output-layout.md`:

```yaml
description: Where ascribe build writes each [build](../reference/content-model/output.md#16-buildsname)'s output, how it records what it wrote, and how it replaces a previous output.
```

`description` is a plain `string` with `role = "description"`, so the brackets and the path are part of the text: they're in the page's `<meta name="description">`, in `llms.txt`, and in the page records. Because it isn't a link, `ascribe rename` doesn't update it when the target moves, and `ascribe check` doesn't report it when it dangles.

It's the only description in `docs/content/` with one.

## What to do

- Take the link out, leaving the word: "Where ascribe build writes each build's output, …".
- Consider a check for it. A description that holds Markdown link syntax is almost certainly a mistake, and it reaches every reader that isn't a person. It would be advice, with a fix that keeps the link's text, beside `description-too-long` and `description-duplicate`. If it's added, it's a new diagnostic with a recorded decision; if not, say so on this issue and close it with the one-line fix.

## How it was found

Moving Ascribe's own docs pages for #452: the rename left this destination alone, and nothing reported it. #452 changed the path by hand, so after it merges the description holds the new path and is still text.

content.body:
The generator that writes the diagnostics reference rewrites link destinations inside code spans, so two examples in the published reference show a path nobody would write.

## What happens

`tests/conformance/tests/docs.rs` writes the diagnostics fragments in `docs/content/_generated/` from `tests/conformance/diagnostics.toml`. Its `rebase_links` makes the registry's relative links resolve from the fragment's folder, by putting a prefix before every destination that follows `](`:

```rust
while let Some(at) = rest.find("](") {
    …
    if !(dest.starts_with('#') || dest.starts_with('{') || dest.contains("://")) {
        out.push_str("../reference/");
    }
```

It doesn't look at whether the `](` is inside a code span. Two `fix` texts have an example there:

| Diagnostic | In the registry | In the generated page, on `main` |
|---|---|---|
| `image-alt-missing` | `` `![The settings page](settings.png)` `` | `` `![The settings page](../reference/settings.png)` `` |
| `image-attribute-missing` | `` `![Alt](image.png){width=600}` `` | `` `![Alt](../reference/image.png){width=600}` `` |

So the reference tells a reader to write `../reference/settings.png` where the example means any image beside the page. `ascribe explain` and `check`'s JSON show the registry's text as written, so they're right, and the reference disagrees with them.

#452 changes what the prefix is, since it moves the docs' pages, and leaves this as it is: the examples will read `../settings.png` after it.

## What should happen

`rebase_links` leaves a destination alone when it's inside a code span. `escape_braces`, a few lines below it in the same file, already tracks code spans by their backtick runs; the same tracking fits here.

## To check with it

- A test for a `fix` text with a link in a code span and a real link beside it: the first is unchanged and the second is rebased.
- Re-bless the fragments (`ASCRIBE_BLESS=1 cargo test -p ascribe-conformance --test docs`) and read the diff: only those two examples should change.
- Whether the same function, or one like it, is used for the other generated fragments that carry registry text.

## How it was found

While moving the docs' pages for #452, re-blessing the fragments changed two examples that should have been untouched.
