The phase records eleven answers before anything ships. Each has a recommendation in the phase file:

1. **`[versions] current`:** removed; `[releases]` replaces it, and a project that sets it gets an error naming `[releases]`. Amends decision 67.
2. **What a line is:** the number as the list writes it; a version is in the line it starts with (`3.4` holds `3.4.2`). Every line of a target has the same number of parts.
3. **The phrase for a target's line:** a phrase the project declares, `version = { line = "ascribe" }`.
4. **"Planned" in three outputs:** a `planned` attribute on the element's target entry, text "Self-managed (planned, 3.6)"; the same text in the plain output; `planned: true` in the JSON. Label set by `[releases] planned-label`.
5. **The shared file:** `<output-dir>/_ascribe/versions.json`, owned through `_ascribe/manifest.json`, written by every build of a project with `[releases]` and removed when the table goes.
6. **A problem in several lines:** said once, with the builds it's in (`site@3.4`), as today; no new `lines` field.
7. **`@ascribed/astro`:** one collection with the line in each entry, ids like `3.4/install`, and a `Versions.astro` component.
8. **The two unnamed commands:** `ascribe versions list` and `ascribe versions changes "<target> <from>" <to>`.
9. **Indexing older lines:** `[listing] older-lines = "unlisted"`, a level at the table's top.
10. **A release in a one-site project:** `release` moves the line before it to `archived` with no address when no build is versioned by the target.
11. **Versions before the window:** a line's output leaves out a version at or before the oldest live line; every other build shows it.

Answer each on this issue ("take the recommendation" is an answer). Then it's Ready.

Phase 7 of the versions plan (#500) says `ascribe versions changes` lists a page that `replaces` another as one entry, not a removal and an addition. `replaces` comes with phase 4 (#497, PR #507), which wasn't merged when #500 was built, so `changes` reads the marks alone and doesn't follow it yet.

Once #507 is in `main`: when a page removed between the two lines is replaced by a page added in them, `changes` reports one entry for the pair (in the text, the JSON, and the Markdown draft), and `examples/quill` gains the rewritten page the acceptance criterion names (`ascribe versions changes "self-managed 3.4" 3.5` lists it once).

content.body:
The 0.3.1 hand rewrite (d458f201) changed `{available=next}` at the end of a list item in `docs/content/editor/index.md` to `{available="ascribe 0.3.1"}`. In the language, `{available=...}` is a mark only on a table row, so on a list item it renders as text, and readers see the braces.

Found while comparing `ascribe versions release` with that rewrite (#500): the command rightly leaves it, since it isn't a mark. The fix is to mark that content another way (an `@available` before the block, or a row), or drop the braces.

content.body:
From the review of #515: `ascribe agents index --build site@3.4` on quill (with `agents = true`) gives a heading of `## docs.quill.dev`, while that line's `llms.txt` says `# docs.quill.dev (self-managed 3.4)` (decision 57 in `project-docs/versions/README.md`). An index pasted into a product's `AGENTS.md` is read without its address bar, so it should name the line too, the same way `llms.txt` does, for a build with more than one live line.

Where: `crates/ascribe-resolve/src/llms.rs` (`compact_index`, and `line_header`, which `llms_files` uses), called from `crates/ascribe-query/src/agents_index.rs`.

content.body:
Found reviewing #523 (decision 84 in the [versions plan](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/versions/README.md)).

## What happens

With `live = ["3.4", "3.5"]` for `self-managed` and only a versioned build, `ascribe check` reports `self-managed 3.4.2` as ASC212 `available-same-in-every-line` ("no output shows them; write `self-managed`"), with a fix marked `safe`.

But a line's output does show it. The conformance case `builds/lines/versions-before-the-window` expects `site@3.4` and `site@3.5` to keep `self-managed 3.4.2`, since SPEC §9.3 hides only a version "at or before the oldest live line", and 3.4.2 is after 3.4. So applying the safe fix changes both lines' badges.

The cause is in `inert_issues` (`crates/ascribe-check/src/releases.rs`): `at_or_before` counts a version that is in the oldest line (`in_line(oldest, v)`) as well as one before it. `ascribe_core::availability::without_versions_through`, which line outputs and `ascribe versions retire` use, compares with `v.compare(oldest).is_le()` and keeps 3.4.2.

To reproduce: copy that conformance case, delete its `[builds.badges]` build, and run `ascribe check`.

## Done looks like

- ASC212 isn't reported, and no fix is offered, for a version inside the oldest line but newer than it (`3.4.1`, `3.4.2` with 3.4 the oldest), or for a history step at one.
- A version at or before the oldest line (`3.4`, `3.3`) is still reported as now.
- Preferably, the check decides what's hidden with the same function line outputs use, `without_versions_through`, so the two can't disagree again.
- A test in `ascribe-check` covers the patch-version case. The diagnostic's text in `tests/conformance/diagnostics.toml`, and the docs that describe it (`docs/content/versions/index.md`, `docs/content/content-model/content.md`), still read correctly.
content.title: `available-same-in-every-line` offers to drop a patch version of the oldest line, which a line's output shows

Since #556 (phase 4 of the [Memos plan](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/memos/phase-4-templates.md)), a template's instructions to the writer are memos, and memos are never published. Several template sections are now only a heading and a memo, for example concept's "Use cases", reference's "\{Reference description}", and troubleshooting's "Symptom 1", "Cause 1 of symptom 1", and "Solution or workaround to cause 1 of symptom 1". When a page made from one of these templates leaves such a section unfilled, it builds as a heading with nothing under it. `template-placeholder-left` reports nothing there, because the section has no placeholder left. Before #556, the instruction was a placeholder, and the check reported it.

Raised in the review of #556; the maintainer asked for this issue.

**What might help,** one of:
- **Template-scoped:** on a page of a type with a template, advice for a section that the template gives no content but a memo, and that the page still leaves empty, with nothing in it but memos and directives such as `@id`. This could be a variant of `template-placeholder-left` or a diagnostic of its own. It targets exactly this gap, and reports nothing on pages without a template.
- **General:** advice for any section with no content, subsections included, on any page. This is wider, and it needs a rule for what counts as empty. A `##` heading followed directly by `###` is common and fine, so only a section with nothing in its whole extent would count.

**Done looks like:** a decision on which one (or neither), recorded with the change. If it's a diagnostic or a variant, the change adds its registry entry, a conformance case built from a template section that is only a heading and a memo, and its docs, including the templates guide's "What the check finds".

Out of scope: changing the templates' words, or moving memos so these sections get a placeholder back.

The VS Code integration test "applies them on save where editor.codeActionsOnSave asks" (`packages/vscode/test/integration/suite/actions.it.ts`, under "the page's safe fixes", added by E3 in #563) fails some of the time on `main`. Found by the reviewer of M6 (#561).

**Where it failed:** CI on `main`'s merge of #563 (b7cf39ad), job [js / VS Code extension integration tests](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/actions/runs/38998336316/job/117295765998). It passed on a re-run.

```
1) the editor's actions
     the page's safe fixes
       applies them on save where editor.codeActionsOnSave asks:
  AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: The expression evaluated to a falsy value:
    assert.ok(await editor.document.save())
```

So `TextDocument.save()` resolved `false`. VS Code returns that when the document isn't dirty or the save didn't happen. I haven't confirmed a cause; these are guesses to check first:
- The test before it ("applies them with Source Action") leaves `keys.md` edited and unsaved, so the two tests share the document's state.
- The save participant (`codeActionsOnSave`) races the configuration update. Or the participant runs past `files.participants.timeout` while the language server is still answering, and the save is cancelled.
- The file on disk changed under the editor (the previous test's clean-up), so the save hit a conflict.

**Done looks like:**
- Reproduce the failure, for example by running the suite in a loop or making the language server slow. Name the cause in the pull request.
- Fix the cause in the test, or in the extension if it's a real bug there. Each test in "the page's safe fixes" starts from `keys.md` as it is on disk and leaves it that way.
- Don't skip, retry, or loosen the test's assertions. Waiting on a real condition (the configuration applied, the diagnostics in) is fine. A bare sleep isn't.

The VS Code integration tests run in CI only, so show the fixed test passing in several CI runs from the branch.

Follow-up from the review of #568 (E4, This page whole). Two rows in `crates/ascribe-lsp/src/page_rows.rs` repeat a check's decision rather than sharing it, and can disagree with it:

1. **Review** warns "overdue" whenever the review date is before today, without looking at `checks.is_off(REVIEW_OVERDUE)`. A project that turns `review-overdue` off still gets the warning icon. "Overdue" stays true there; the warning shouldn't show.
2. **Description** shows "missing" with a warning whenever the page's own frontmatter has no non-empty string. `page-description-missing` is narrower: it says nothing for a field with a `default` (the page has the default's description), for a `required` field (that's `frontmatter-missing-field`), or for a non-string value (`frontmatter-type-mismatch`). So a type whose description has a default warns "missing" on every page that leans on it, and the docs' "when the page leaves it empty" doesn't hold.

What fixes both: have each row get its answer from the check's own code, or from a function that code shares, rather than a copy of its condition. The Description row should measure the default when there is one, and keep "missing" for where the check reports it. The Review row should warn only when `review-overdue` is on. Extend `crates/ascribe-cli/tests/all/page_parity.rs` with a project that turns the check off and a type whose description has a default.

**1. "applies them with Source Action, and leaves the rest"** (the page's safe fixes), seen twice, once before and once after #567's change:

```
AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Timed out waiting for the fixes
```

`editor.action.sourceAction` with `{ kind: "source.fixAll.ascribe", apply: "first" }` ran after the diagnostics were in. The server answered the code action requests in a few milliseconds, but no edit was applied. The trace logs (at `messages`, not `verbose`) don't show whether the answer had the fix-all action, or whether VS Code dropped the manual trigger for a newer automatic one. Not confirmed; to check first: VS Code's code action model replaces a pending manual trigger when the editor's markers change, and both Ascribe and the Markdown extension publish diagnostics for `keys.md`.

**2. "lists the fixes for a problem at the cursor first"** (the actions bar), seen once, after #567:

```
AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Expected values to be strictly equal:
+ '-- Structure'
- '-- Fix'
```

The bar opened with no fixes for the `{flush}` problem at the cursor, though the test had waited for its diagnostic.

**Done looks like:** reproduce each with the LSP trace at `verbose` (`"ascribe.trace.server": "verbose"` in the suite's settings in `test/integration/run.ts`, `--log trace` in its `launchArgs`, and the run's `user-data/logs` kept on failure), name the cause, and fix it in the test or the extension, with no skip, retry, or sleep.

Split out of #538 (navigation phase 3, PR #577), whose acceptance criteria include: "The agents' hook settles `nav-page-unplaced` after an agent adds a page."

PR #577 makes `nav-page-unplaced` configurable advice on the new page, with a safe fix that appends it to its section's `pages` in `ascribe.nav`. content.body:
Two tests in `crates/ascribe-cli/tests/all/hook.rs` failed together on Windows in CI and passed on a re-run. Both fail the same timing assertion in `served()`:
- `hook::the_check_server_answers_and_stops_with_its_project`
- `hook::an_edit_to_an_included_fragment_reports_the_page_that_includes_it`

**Where:** PR #577's CI, first attempt, job [rust / clippy and test (windows-latest)](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/actions/runs/39047014622/job/117437670021). The second attempt passed.

```
---- hook::the_check_server_answers_and_stops_with_its_project stdout ----
thread '...' panicked at crates\ascribe-cli\tests\all\hook.rs:73:9:
the hook took 17.9449395s
---- hook::an_edit_to_an_included_fragment_reports_the_page_that_includes_it stdout ----
thread '...' panicked at crates\ascribe-cli\tests\all\hook.rs:73:9:
the hook took 19.0301207s
```

The assertion (`started.elapsed() < 15s`) is there to catch a check server that keeps the hook's output open and holds the agent up. That's a real property worth testing. But wall-clock time on a busy Windows runner can't tell "the output was held open" from "the machine was slow": both tests ran at the same time and both took 18 to 19 seconds.

**Done looks like:**
- The test still fails if the server keeps the hook's standard output open after answering, and no longer fails because the runner is slow. One way: assert on what holding the output open looks like (the hook's output closing, or the hook process exiting, independently of the server's lifetime) rather than on elapsed time. Or measure only the part the server controls.
- If a time bound stays, it bounds something the hook controls, with a margin that holds on a loaded Windows runner. Say in a comment why it's that number.
- Don't skip, retry, or `#[ignore]` the tests.
- Show the tests passing on Windows in CI, ideally in a few runs from the branch.

Cause: `Named::find` returns `Usable::Term` (`crates/ascribe-resolve/src/named.rs:149`); `place` refuses a quote on any entry (`crates/ascribe-lsp/src/memos.rs:418` and the check's equivalent); outline's listing and the language server's memo lookup match only files and headings.

3. **A heading in an included fragment, written `page.md#id`.** `id_edits` matches `path == file`, where links follow the page heading through the include.
4. **An `about` written as a YAML block scalar, or on the line after its key.** `value_span` looks only on the key's line, so the rewrite is skipped silently.

- "bolt" builds as `[bolt](/glossary/#spanner "A spanner is a tool.")`: the other term's heading and definition.

Found reviewing the [roadmap](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/roadmap.md)'s plans after their phases merged, on `main` at b91427ec. Navigation plan, phase 5's criterion that "the sidebar `sidebar()` draws has the view's order", and decision 24.

With pages `a.md`, `guides.md`, and `b.md` at the content root and a folder `guides/`, the Pages view draws Start as Home, Alpha, then the `guides/` section, then Beta. `sidebar()`, `llms.txt`, and `nav.json` give Start (Home, Alpha, Beta), then Guides as a section of its own. #584 made a page beside a top folder read with that folder's section after #583 had shipped the view, and the view didn't follow (`packages/vscode/src/ui/sidebar.ts`, around 123-136 and 186-196). `changes/editor/pages-navigation.md` says Pages shows pages "in the order a sidebar shows them". No unit test has a page beside a top folder.

What fixes it: draw such a section at the top level, after Start, as `nav.json` has it, and decide what dragging it does there (it can't move inside Start's pages). A unit test of `pagesRoots` with a page beside a top folder, compared against the server's `nav.json` for the same project.


## Decided

By the maintainer, 18 October 2026: **a top section is ordered among the top sections by `[[sections]]`, whether or not its own page sits beside its folder, and dragging it in Pages reorders it there.**

- **The top level.** Today a top section whose own page is beside its folder (`guides.md` beside `guides/`) takes its place from where that page would sit among the root's pages, before every other top section, and its `[[sections]]` entry is ignored (`crates/ascribe-resolve/src/navigation.rs`, the `placed` partition). Since #584 that page is the section's own page, shown in no list a writer sees, so nothing visible orders the section. Change the resolver so that at the root no section is placed by a page beside its folder: every top section follows `[[sections]]`, then path order. Pages then draws it as a top section after Start, as `nav.json` does, and a drag writes `[[sections]]` as for any top section.
- **Below the top level, placement stays** as the navigation plan's decision 24 says: `checks/diagnostics/` sits where `diagnostics.md` sits among `checks/`'s pages, which is how a split page keeps its parts in place. Dragging such a section in Pages moves its page beside the folder within the parent's `pages`, instead of being refused, so the same drag does the same visible thing at every depth.
- **The record.** This narrows decision 24 to sections below the root. Say so in SPEC §7.8, the navigation reference and `navigation/order.md`, with a decision file in the pull request. It settles the top-level half of #613's first part; #613 keeps the rest (the reference's wording below the root, `nav-section-unplaced` on a placed section, and sorting titles by their plain text).

Tests: a resolver test that a top section with its page beside its folder follows `[[sections]]`; a `pagesRoots` unit test that draws it after Start; drag tests for a top section and for a placed nested section.

content.body:
Follow-up from #619 (review note: https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/pull/619#discussion_r4307736519).

Since #619, the VS Code extension tells a project's server about a change to any file in its sources' folders, wherever they are (`toldOfChange` in `packages/vscode/src/diskChanges.ts`), skipping only `node_modules` and `.git`. For Ascribe's own docs the source is `path = ".."`, so the docs' server now hears about everything under the repository's root, including `target/` during a `cargo build`.

On the server, `did_change_watched` (`crates/ascribe-lsp/src/core.rs`) asks for every lens again for any path in a source's folder (`shown::in_a_source` ignores `include`), and `collect_present` walks a created directory. So a build can send the docs' server a stream of lens refreshes and directory walks it didn't get before.

What done looks like: a change under a source's folder reaches the server, and refreshes its lenses, only when the server can use it: a file the source's `include` patterns cover, or the source's `ascribe.examples.toml` and observations. Files elsewhere in the folder (such as `target/`) send nothing. A unit test for a file outside `include` in a source's folder, and a language server test that an event for such a file asks for no refresh.

content.body:
`ascribe render` doesn't render: it writes plain Markdown, and the name promises something visual. The [docs audit](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/docs-audit.md) read it that way ("`render` is plain Markdown. It can't show tabs, badges, or the lens"), and inside the codebase "render" means HTML: `render_site_html`, the preview, and AGENTS.md's "Two renderers must agree". The name was never weighed: the agents plan's phase 2 took it from the code it calls (`ascribe_query::render`, which calls `emit_page`).

What the command does is SPEC §9.1's two middle stages for one page: it **resolves** the page for one build (§9.2: includes and snippets, availability, the build's variants, phrases, heading ids, links), then writes it with the plain emitter, as `ascribe build --emit plain` would. Its output is the page's Markdown version, the `.md` file a site with `[consumer] agents = true` publishes for agents.

## The change

- **`ascribe render` becomes `ascribe resolve`,** with the same arguments, options, exit codes, and output. Its help says what it writes: "Resolves a page for one build and writes it as the build's plain Markdown output."
- **The MCP tool `ascribe_render` becomes `ascribe_resolve`,** by the checklist's rule that a tool is named for its command.
- **Its JSON document's schema becomes `resolve.schema.json`,** with `schema_version` still `1` and no field changed.
- **No alias.** Ascribe is before 1.0, and a project changes with it.

## Decided

- The maintainer chose the name on 20 October 2026: `resolve`, over keeping `render` and adding HTML, or folding the command into `ascribe build`. The tool's name and the JSON document are contracts (decisions 52 and 56), so the pull request adds a decision file in `project-docs/decisions/`, named by this issue, that renames them.

## Where it's named

About 105 mentions in 40 files outside `CHANGELOG.md` (`git grep -E "ascribe render|ascribe_render"`):

- the CLI (`crates/ascribe-cli/src/cli.rs`, `commands/render.rs`), the entry (`crates/ascribe-query/src/render.rs`), the tool (`crates/ascribe-cli/src/mcp/tools.rs`), and `shapes.rs` with the schema in `schemas/`;
- the agent skill (`crates/ascribe-cli/src/agents/skill.rs`, and its copies in `packages/cli/skills/` and `plugins/ascribe/`, rewritten by their tests), and `diff`'s agent prompts (`crates/ascribe-diff/src/prompt.rs`) with their snapshots and `crates/ascribe-cli/tests/output/`;
- the docs: `docs/content/command/questions.md` (the section, its `cli-render` permalink, and the page's title), `agents/index.md`, `agents/commands.md`, `review/diff.md`, `versions/index.md`, `writing/variants.md`, `contracts/json-reports/questions.md`, and the generated files rewritten from the help text;
- the records that describe the current command: decisions #502d, #502e, and #502g, and the search proposal. Plans and audits that describe what was true when they were written stay as they are.

The `cli-render` permalink is published, so it's retired to the new section, as `ascribe permalinks retire` does, not removed.

## Done when

- `ascribe resolve` answers as `ascribe render` did, and `ascribe render` is an unknown command.
- `ascribe_resolve` is the tool, and `ascribe_render` isn't.
- `git grep -E "ascribe render|ascribe_render|render\.schema"` finds only the changelog, the new decision file, and records of what was.
- `ascribe agents sync --check` passes in the repository, and the release notes' entry in `changes/` says agent files synced before it name the old command until `ascribe agents sync` runs again.

## Coordination

The search plan's first phase, #641, holds search's reading to "what `ascribe render` writes". Whichever merges second updates the other's mention.

The brainstorm's section 22 keeps what the rename leaves for later: `--emit site`, and HTML.

The weekly corpora run has failed on main since run 8 (https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/actions/runs/38263080573, and again in https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/actions/runs/39250005898). `tests/corpora/tests/recognition.rs` fails because two classes the corpora now produce have no entry in `tests/corpora/recognition.toml`:

- `diagnostic:html-comment`, in all three corpora (Astro, Docker, Elastic). For example `recipes/sharing-state-islands.mdx:226:1 <!--src/components/CartFlyoutToggle.vue-->` and `guides/testcontainers-go-getting-started.md:20:1 <!-- Source: … -->`.
- `diagnostic:frontmatter-reserved-in-fragment`, in Elastic only: `contribute-docs/content-types/_snippets/templates/how-to-template.md:6:1 type: how-to`, and the same in `overview-template.md` and `troubleshooting-template.md`.

Each needs a verdict (`intended`, or `false-positive` naming a finding in FINDINGS.md). The second one may be a false positive: those files are templates under `_snippets/` whose front matter is part of the text they show.

Because the test step fails, the benchmarks never run, so no perf baseline can be recorded until this is fixed. #664 (search phase 1) needs its `search/synthetic-3000` baseline recorded and is blocked on this.

content.body:
`available-same-in-every-line` reports a mark whose versions are all at or before the oldest live line, and offers the simpler spec. It reports nothing in a project that shows badges: `shown` in `crates/ascribe-check/src/releases.rs` counts any build with `availability = "badge"` as one that shows the mark, and the check only reports marks no output shows. So a badge build keeps "Ascribe 0.2.0" badges for as long as the source says so, and nothing points at them.

Found by the [docs audit](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/docs-audit.md) ("Marks and badges the release left behind"). Ascribe's own docs build `site` with badges and no `versions`, and their live line is 0.4.0; `git grep -c "@available: ascribe 0\.[23]" -- docs/content` counts 191 marks, 27 of them 0.2, and they head a third of the home page's list.

## The change

In a build that shows badges, a mark every live line of its target has, with its last state available, is reported as advice: the badge it makes says only that the content is older than every live line. The same condition `available-same-in-every-line` uses today, with the one difference that the mark is shown.

- **One diagnostic, a second message.** `available-same-in-every-line` gains a message for this case in `tests/conformance/diagnostics.toml`'s `messages`, saying what's true here: the badge is shown, and says nothing a reader of any live line needs. The existing message ("so no output shows them") stays for the case it describes.
- **Its fix is `unsafe` here.** The simpler spec removes the badge, so it changes what the page says, and a fix is `safe` only when it can't (decision 51). Where no output shows the mark, it stays `safe`.
- **Advice, and configurable as it is.** Some teams keep "new in 0.2" for good, as Python's docs do; `[checks] available-same-in-every-line = "off"` keeps their badges quiet.

A behavior change, so it comes with a conformance case: a badge build, a mark older than the oldest live line reported with the new message and an unsafe fix, and a mark in a live line not reported.

## Ascribe's own docs

This issue adds the check that finds the marks. Removing them from the docs is the audit's own work (its "Order of work", item 1); until then `ascribe check` on the docs lists them as advice, which `--deny-warnings` doesn't fail on.

## Done when

- The conformance case passes, and `ascribe check --config docs` reports the docs' old marks with the badge message.
- `docs/content/checks/diagnostics/` says what the check reports in a badge build, and an entry in `changes/` says so.
content.title: Old availability marks aren't reported in a build that shows badges

content.body:
`ascribe refs` can't say where an image is used. From `docs/`, `ascribe refs images/review-site-preview.png` answers "doesn't exist", for the image [Review](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/docs/content/review/index.md) shows; so does the path from the repository's root. Found by the [docs audit](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/docs-audit.md) ("The tools", "Fell short").

A target of `refs` is a source file or a content model entry (`Named` in `crates/ascribe-resolve/src/named.rs`). An image is neither, so it's read as a source that isn't there. The uses are already known: `image-unused` reads them (`images` in `crates/ascribe-check/src/across.rs`), from the pages and fragments that show or link to the image (`asset_users`), and the raw HTML and frontmatter fields that name it (`mentioned_paths`).

## The change

- **An image under the content root is a target,** named as a source is: a path from the current folder, or from the content root.
- **Its places** are each file that shows it, links to it, or names it in raw HTML or a frontmatter field, each with its `use`. `image` and `html` and `frontmatter` are new values of `use`, an addition to the JSON document under decision 4, with the schema regenerated.
- **An image nothing uses** answers with no places and exit code `0`, as any target that exists does.
- **A file that's neither a source nor an image** says what `refs` takes, instead of "doesn't exist", since it does exist.

The MCP tool's `target` description, and `ascribe refs`' section in `docs/content/command/questions.md`, name images.

## Done when

- The audit's command lists Review's line, from `docs/` and from the repository's root, in tests.
- An unused image answers with no places and `0`, and a file that's neither says so, in tests.
- An entry in `changes/` says `refs` takes an image.

The directive reference's table of built-ins ([`docs/content/writing/directives.md`](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/docs/content/writing/directives.md#built-in-directives), `Directive | Forms | Primary | Purpose`) is written by hand, and a `@memo` above it asks whoever adds a built-in to put it in SPEC §4's order there, in the contents, and in the sections. Nothing compares it with the code. Found by the [docs audit](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/docs-audit.md) (section 5, "The templates").

The code already declares every column: `builtin_schemas()` in `crates/ascribe-core/src/schema.rs` returns each built-in in SPEC §4's order, with its `name`, `forms`, `primary`, whether it's `groupable`, and its `description`, which is the table's Purpose with a full stop. The docs' own template for a reference says a table the code declares is generated into a fragment and kept by a test ([`docs/templates/reference.ascribe.md`](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/docs/templates/reference.ascribe.md)).

## The change

- **The table is generated** from `builtin_schemas()` into `docs/content/_generated/`, as the command reference's options are (`crates/ascribe-cli/src/docs.rs`), included where the table is, and rewritten with `ASCRIBE_BLESS=1`. A test fails when it's stale.
- **Each column comes from the schema:** the forms from `forms` and `groupable` ("line, container", "container, grouped"), the primary from `primary` in the words the table uses now, and Purpose from `description`.
- **A row's availability mark** (`{available="ascribe 0.4.0"}` on `@memo` and `@term` today) needs a home the generator reads, since the schema has none. Say in the pull request where it's kept; a new built-in's row is marked `next` until a release rewrites it.
- **The memo goes,** since the order is the code's. The contents line above the table, which lists the built-ins too, is generated with it or held to it by the same test.

## Done when

- No row of the table is written by hand, and adding a built-in to `Builtin` without regenerating fails a test.
- `ascribe check --config docs` passes.

content.body:
`ascribe model` reports the types, dimensions, phrases, features, glossary, widgets, releases, builds, sources, and navigation, and not `[project]`, `[consumer]`, `[editor]`, `[checks]`, `[crawlers]`, `[listing]`, or `[permalinks]`. The [docs audit](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/docs-audit.md) confirmed those keys from the loader by hand ("The tools", "Fell short"), and an agent has no way to ask for them.

#649 makes one registry of every key of `ascribe.toml`, with its kind and default, which the loader reads. Once it's there, `model` can report every section from it, with the value in effect, the default where the file leaves a key out.

## The change

- **`--section` takes each missing section,** and the MCP tool's `section` argument with it (`model_sections` in `crates/ascribe-cli/src/mcp/tools.rs`).
- **The JSON document gains each section,** each key with its value in effect. Fields are added and none changes meaning, so `schema_version` stays `1`, under decision 4.
- **The default text stays within 4,000 characters** (decision 52): the new sections are shown with `--section`, and the summary names them where it names what it cut.
- **The keys and defaults come from the registry,** never a second list, so `model` can't show a key the loader refuses.

## Done when

- `ascribe model --section consumer --config docs` shows `[consumer]`'s keys with their values and defaults, and the JSON has every section, in tests.
- `ascribe model`'s text without `--section` is still within 4,000 characters.
- `ascribe model`'s section in `docs/content/command/questions.md` lists the sections, and an entry in `changes/` says so.

**Needs:** #649.

Phase D18 of [the docs after the audit](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/docs-cleanup/README.md#pictures). The spec is this phase's entry there and the sections of the [docs audit](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/docs-audit.md) it names, under the plan's rules for every phase. **Done when** below is what done looks like, and it's one pull request.

**Done when:** each picture is on its page with alt text that says what its cut paragraph said, its prose is cut, and the freshness test covers it; a scene the script can't reach is taken by hand, says so in the pull request, and has the same record, so the test covers it too.

**A picture has a text form.** Its alt text says in a sentence what the cut paragraph said, so a reader with a screen reader loses nothing: decision 46's "nothing is told by color alone" holds for a picture too. `image-alt-missing` is the check that holds an image to having one; the review of each phase holds the sentence to saying what the picture shows.

**Decided:**
- Decision 4 of [the plan](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/docs-cleanup/README.md#decisions): **The pictures: scripted or by hand.** **Decided:** scripted. The editor's picture already is: `packages/vscode/scripts/screenshot.ts` takes it, and `scripts/docs-site/screenshots.ts` keeps its record and the command that retakes it, with `scripts/docs-site/screenshots.test.ts` failing one minor release behind. So the scenes extend a harness that exists. The risk is reach: a hover, a peek, and a status bar in several states are scenes a script has to drive, not only open. A scene the script can't reach falls back to a picture taken by hand with the same record, so the staleness test holds either way.

**Needs:** nothing.

content.body:
With the recognition verdicts fixed (#666), the corpora run now reaches the benchmarks, and `benches/perf.rs` panics in `one_file` for the converted Elastic sample (https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/actions/runs/39482480876/job/118834319380):

```
thread 'main' panicked at tests/corpora/benches/perf.rs:290:10:
a clean page
```

content.body:
Found reviewing #664 (Search phase 1). The maintainer agreed it's a follow-up, not part of that PR.

## What happens

`ascribe_resolve::reading::find` matches each block once, at its first match. When that first match falls wholly inside a phrase's value, `locate` turns it into the phrase's place in `ascribe.toml` and never looks at the rest of the block. The line's own text is then missing from the results, even where it matches the query too.

In `examples/quill`, `ascribe search quill` lists `ascribe.toml:34` (the `cloud` phrase) but not `docs/install-agent.md:62`. That line says ``Sign in to {cloud} and copy an API key … then add it to `quill.yaml` ``: the first `quill` is inside `{cloud}`'s value, and the `quill.yaml` after it is never found. `docs/keys.md:10` drops out the same way. Someone searching `quill` to find every mention of `quill.yaml` misses those lines.

## What done looks like

- When a block's first match is wholly inside a phrase's value, the phrase's place is still recorded, and matching carries on in the same block after that phrase. A match that isn't wholly in a phrase makes the line a place of its own, as `project-docs/search/phase-1-thread.md`'s "From a match to a place" describes.
- `ascribe search quill` in `examples/quill` lists `docs/install-agent.md:62` and `docs/keys.md:10`, as well as the phrase's line.
- A test in `crates/ascribe-resolve/tests/all/reading.rs` covers a block whose first match is in a phrase and whose later match is in its own text.
- The phase file says the rule, if the fix changes what it says.

Phase V6 of the [editor's next views](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/roadmap.md#track-v-the-project-view), split from V2 (#655) by the roadmap's decision 9. The spec is this phase's entry there and the sections of the [Project view proposal](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/proposals/project-view.md) it names. **Done when** below is what done looks like, and it's one pull request.

**Done when:** `ascribe observe` in a terminal shows its commands and runs nothing when declined, with `--yes` it doesn't ask, and without a terminal it runs as today, in tests; the task runs in each such source's folder, in Run Task and the Project view; the extension reads no TOML to find the sources or the commands; the docs (`docs/content/examples/tested.md`, the command's reference) say how the question works; and AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, and RELEASING.md, which tell people to run `ascribe observe`, say what it asks.

**Decided:**
- Decision 9 of the [roadmap](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/roadmap.md#decisions): **How Observe Examples asks before it runs.** V2's pull request (#735) found that `ascribe observe` takes no `--config` and runs only the `ascribe.examples.toml` in the folder it's run from, and built the question as a modal in front of a hand-built terminal, with the sources and commands read from TOML by the extension. **Decided:** `ascribe observe` asks for itself. When standard input is a terminal, it shows the commands it will run, from its own reading of the file, and asks before running them; `--yes` skips the question; where standard input isn't a terminal, as in CI or a hook, it runs as today. The Observe Examples task is then a plain process, as Build and Sync Agent Files are, run in the folder of each source with tested examples, which the extension learns from the binary (the model's JSON), parsing no TOML of its own. A change to the CLI's behavior, so V6 adds a decision file and a test of the question.

**Needs:** #655.

The review of #735, which first built this, says what to avoid: a `Pseudoterminal` in front of the process, and the extension reading `ascribe.toml` and `ascribe.examples.toml` itself.

The rest of phase V2 of the [editor's next views](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/roadmap.md#track-v-the-project-view) (#655), split out in review of #735, which ships Build and Sync Agent Files. The spec is V2's entry and the Project view proposal's "Observe Examples runs commands the repository names".

**Done when:** Observe Examples runs `ascribe observe` as an `ascribe` task, offered only in a trusted workspace, showing the commands it will run and asking before each run, with nothing in the extension that keeps a second copy of what the binary knows (which sources have tested examples, or which commands observe runs).

**Needs a decision from the maintainer before it's Ready:**

1. **Where it runs.** The roadmap says each task runs "in the project's folder, with `--config`". `ascribe observe` takes no `--config` and runs only the `ascribe.examples.toml` in the folder it's run from, so it has to run in the folder of a source with tested examples. The review of #735 agreed that's right, and that the roadmap's wording is what's wrong; it needs to be recorded as the maintainer's call, along with how `tasks.json` names which source (a `source` property was proposed).
2. **How its question is asked.** Two shapes from the review:
   - **A:** `ascribe observe` shows the commands it will run and asks when standard input is a terminal, with `--yes` to skip; CI isn't a terminal and is unchanged. The task is then a `ProcessExecution` like Build's, and the question can't drift from what runs. A CLI behavior change: a decision file and a conformance case.
   - **B:** the extension keeps a modal, taking the sources from the binary (the model's JSON, `ModelSource` in `crates/ascribe-query/src/model.rs`, or the language server) and the commands from a new `ascribe observe --list`. The pseudoterminal stays.
3. **"The editor never runs it."** `docs/content/examples/tested.md` says the editor never runs `ascribe observe`, and `packages/vscode/test/unit/manifest.test.ts` holds to it. Observe Examples replaces that, which is the maintainer's to record.

**Needs:** #655 (#735)

The VS Code integration test "opens a snippet's file and a tested example's beside the page, with This page still on it" (`packages/vscode/test/integration/suite/tested.it.ts:117`, added in #727 for #652) has failed on CI on six pull requests and once on `main` since it landed on 21 October, and passes when the job is run again. It almost always fails the same way: it presses the `@snippet` row for `code/examples/greet.out.txt` in This page, and the file never opens beside the page within `waitFor`'s 30 seconds.

```
1) a code file a page shows
     opens a snippet's file and a tested example's beside the page, with This page still on it:
   AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Timed out waiting for /tmp/tv-tGsL5Q/workspace/code/examples/greet.out.txt beside the page
	at waitFor (out/integration/suite/tested.it.cjs:45:39)
```

It's the first of the test's two rows, so the press is lost before anything opens. The other tests in the `tested` suite pass in the same runs, including "lists the page's tested examples in This page", which reads the same rows.

## Where it failed

Every one is the "VS Code extension integration tests" job, failing in suite `tested`:

| Pull request | Commit | Run | Failure |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #733 (docs only) | `d68e5130` | [attempt 1](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/actions/runs/39529023628/job/118990703674), [attempt 2](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/actions/runs/39529023628/job/118995955929) | `greet.out.txt` timeout, twice |
| #729 | `ed36a37f` | [run](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/actions/runs/39528995869/job/118990312193) | `greet.out.txt` timeout |
| #740 | `8767fabe` | [attempt 1](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/actions/runs/39530379375/job/118997075855) | `greet.out.txt` timeout; attempt 2 passed |
| `main`, the merge of #732 | `a4ea6dcc` | [run](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/actions/runs/39531928059/job/119001380899) | `greet.out.txt` timeout |
| #736 | `9d383e64` | [run](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/actions/runs/39535697272/job/119011745179) | `greet.out.txt` timeout |
| #742 | `af72ea82` | [attempt 1](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/actions/runs/39538700099/job/119021718069) | `greet.out.txt` timeout (with another failure, in Search) |
| #743 | `d304d748` | [attempt 1](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/actions/runs/39542311876/job/119032645263), [attempt 2](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/actions/runs/39542311876/job/119034985606) | timeout, then the variant below |

Attempt 2 on #743 failed one step later: the file opened, but This page's focused row was gone afterwards.

```
AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Expected values to be strictly equal:
+ actual - expected

+ null
- 'connections/2/1'
```

That's `assert.equal(after.report.focused, key)`, after `view.whenSettled()`. So the page's update can drop the focus, as well as the press being lost.

## What it isn't

#743's implementor thought the cause was a race with the task provider's `ascribe model` call at activation, and made the extension ask for the tested sources once (`e491738`). That doesn't explain it. Both #743 failures are on `d304d748`, which is before that commit, and the failures on #729, #733, #736, #740 and `main` are before #743 was opened. The test was flaky from the start.

Things worth looking at instead: whether `view.probe({ open: true, focus: key, press: true })` can arrive before the webview has drawn the rows the key names, or while a redraw replaces them (`whenDrawn` waits for the Health section, not for Connections); and whether a redraw after the page loses focus to the new editor resets `focused`.

## Done when

- The pull request explains why the press was lost (and why the focus was dropped in the second failure), from a trace or from logging added for it, not a guess.
- The fix is in the extension or in what the test waits for. It doesn't add a retry or raise the timeout.
- The `tested` suite passes in at least 10 runs of the integration job in a row on the pull request's last commit (run it with `workflow_dispatch` or reruns, and link them).

content.body:
Follow-ups from the review of #753 (https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/pull/753#pullrequestreview-5599977160), notes 1 to 3, all non-blocking there.

#753 (for #745) moved what `report links` remembers from `actions/cache` to an artifact of each run. `.github/workflows/report.yml` lists the newest `ascribe-links` artifact with `gh api`, then downloads it with `gh run download`. `docs/content/checks/report.md` ("On a schedule") publishes that job to users through its `:snippet-start: job` markers, so what's fixed here is fixed for them too.

## What's wrong

1. **A failed download stops the report.** If `gh api` or `gh run download` fails, for example on a transient API error or an artifact that expired between the list and the download, the step fails and `Report` never runs. A cache miss used to be harmless: the report ran with nothing remembered.
2. **The artifact's root is the paths' common folder.** `upload-artifact` stores files relative to the folder that `docs/.ascribe/cache` and `docs/.ascribe/history` share. If one of them were missing or empty, the other's files would be stored without their folder name, and download straight into `docs/.ascribe/`.
3. **"when asked twice" can be wrong.** The persistent-5xx message says "answered 5xx … when asked twice" even when the second ask failed to run. In that case the first answer stands and still matches `is_server_error`.

## Done when

- If listing or downloading the artifact fails, the step warns (`::warning::`, saying that every failure will be reported) and the report still runs with nothing remembered. Nothing else in the job changes.
- What's uploaded downloads back to `docs/.ascribe/cache/…` and `docs/.ascribe/history/…` even when only one of the two folders has files. For example, upload `docs/.ascribe` with only those two folders included, or give the upload a fixed root. The pull request shows the artifact's file list from a `workflow_dispatch` run.
- A 5xx is described as "when asked twice" only when it was asked twice. If the second ask didn't run, the message doesn't say so. A test in `crates/ascribe-check/tests/all/link_retry.rs` covers the case. The JSON's fields don't change.
- `docs/content/checks/report.md` still builds from the snippet and describes the download's fallback.

**Ascribe version:** main after #754 (the VS Code extension)

**Platform:** any

**What happened, and what you expected:**

#754 made This page's webview give the focus back to the row that had it last when the window gets the focus back and nothing in the view has it (`packages/vscode/src/webview/thisPage.ts`, the window `focus` listener, which calls `focusKey(lastFocused)`).

The window's `focus` event fires on the mousedown when a reader clicks into This page from an editor, before the row they clicked takes the focus. If the row that had the focus last has been scrolled out of view, `focusKey` calls `target.focus()`, which scrolls that row back into view first. The content can then move under the pointer between mousedown and mouseup, so the click lands on a different row, or on nothing. (Found in review of #754: https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/pull/754#discussion_r4338395725)

Expected: the click lands on the row the reader aimed at, and restoring the focus never scrolls the view.

**Done when:**

- `focusKey` takes an option to focus without scrolling (`focus({ preventScroll: true })`), and the window `focus` restore uses it.
- Keyboard moves, the redraw restore, and the integration probe still scroll the focused row into view as they do now.
- A test covers it: a unit or webview test that the window `focus` restore doesn't change the view's scroll position, or an integration case that scrolls the last-focused row out of view, clicks another row from the editor, and opens that row.
- The `tested` integration suite still passes in CI.

**The smallest input that shows it:** any page with enough rows in This page to scroll. Focus a row, scroll it out of view, click into an editor, then click a different row in This page.

The VS Code integration test "sets the trailing slash to never in one line, unsaved, and follows Undo in the file" (`packages/vscode/test/integration/suite/settings.it.ts`) failed once on #763's first CI run and passed on the next run, with only a merge from `main` between the two. Found by #763's reviewer.

**Where it failed:** [CI run 39630339876](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/actions/runs/39630339876), job "js / VS Code extension integration tests":

```
1) sets the trailing slash to never in one line, unsaved, and follows Undo in the file:
   Error: Timed out waiting for Project Settings to draw the trailing slash, always
```

The five tests after it then failed because `ascribe.toml` still read `trailing-slash = "never"`. So the `undo` command didn't change the document at all; the tab had no change to draw.

**Likely cause (not confirmed):** the test before it ends with `ascribe.openProjectSettings`, which reveals and focuses the Project Settings panel. The Undo test then calls `showTextDocument(document, { viewColumn: Two })` and runs `undo` straight after. If focus hasn't reached the editor yet, `undo` goes to the webview and does nothing. The next test, which comes from an editor that already has focus, undoes three edits without trouble in the same run.

**Done looks like:**
- Reproduce the failure, or show the focus race. Name the cause in the pull request.
- Fix the cause in the test, or in the extension if it's a real bug there. For example, wait until the editor actually has focus, or undo through something tied to the document instead of the focused element.
- Don't skip, retry, or loosen the test's assertions. Waiting on a real condition is fine. A bare sleep isn't.

The VS Code integration tests run in CI only, so show the fixed test passing in several CI runs from the branch.

content.body:
A follow-up to the Project view as 0.4.1 shipped it ([proposal](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/62bf76a9/project-docs/proposals/project-view.md), [docs](https://ascribed-dev.com/docs/editor/sidebar/#the-project-view)). **Done when** below is what done looks like, and it's one pull request.

**The problem:** each Health count is a label beside its value, its note, and its action (`.row`: the term at least 7.5em, the value at least 10em, wrapping). A long label pushes the rest under it, each piece at its own indent, so every count reads differently. The four counts from Check Every Build each repeat "Needs every build checked" and their own **Check Every Build** button, though one check brings all four current. "6 things to do" counts each of those four dashes as a thing to do. And Actions sits under Health, whose height changes as the counts do, so the buttons move.

**What to build:** Health's counts in groups by when each is from, the note and the action said once per group, at the group's head; each count one line, its label then its value:

```
Actions
  …
Health                                   2 to do
  Every build · not checked yet    ▷ Check Every Build
    Problems                  —
    Tested examples           —
    Reviews overdue           —
    Permalinks behind         —
  As you type
    Pages nothing links to    0
    Unused model entries      5
  At the last save · 3:30 PM
    Agent files out of date   4
```

- The groups: **Every build** (the last Check Every Build: problems, examples, overdue reviews, permalinks), **As you type** (`ascribe/inventory`: orphans, unused entries), and **At the last save** (`ascribe agents sync --check`: agent files). A group's head says its state as the counts' notes say it now (not checked yet, checking, checked at a time, out of date and why, couldn't finish), and carries its action while the group isn't current.
- Overdue reviews keep their day: when the check is current but from another day, that count alone is a dash, with its own note ("checked on 20 October; reviews fall due by the day") and the action.
- "To do" counts the current counts above zero, as the mock's 2 (unused entries, agent files). A group that isn't current isn't a thing to do: its head says so, with its action.
- The sections' order is the head, then **Actions**, **Health**, and **About**, Actions open at first as now.
- A count still says what it is in words, never by color alone (decision 46): a dash keeps its group's note as its accessible name, as the value's `aria-label` does now.

**Done when:** the view draws the groups and the order above, in `test/webview/` and the view's unit tests (`projectHealth.ts`'s answer); a narrow sidebar wraps a long label without moving its value under the next count's; the four every-build counts show one note and one **Check Every Build**; "to do" follows the rule the docs state; and `docs/content/editor/sidebar.md`'s Project view section describes the groups and the order. The pull request adds a decision file for the order and the groups, since the proposal ordered Health before Actions and gave each count its own note.

content.body:
A follow-up to the Project view as 0.4.1 shipped it ([proposal](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/62bf76a9/project-docs/proposals/project-view.md), "When each count is from"). **Done when** below is what done looks like, and it's one pull request.

**The problem:** the last Check Every Build lives only as long as the window (`src/ui/checkEveryBuild.ts`). Every time VS Code opens, the four counts from it are dashes, "not checked yet", until someone runs it again, though nothing may have changed since yesterday's check. The view rightly never runs the check by itself (the proposal: it takes a second or more on a large project).

**What to build:** the last check's result kept between sessions, per project, in the workspace's storage (`ExtensionContext.workspaceState`), and on opening:

- **Nothing in the project changed since the check started:** its counts are current, as if it had just run, and its problems are back in the Problems panel, so a count still opens the problems it counts. "Checked yesterday at 3:30 PM" says when.
- **Something changed:** a file of the project (its `ascribe.toml`, the files under its content root and its sources' folders, as `isCurrent` follows them) modified after the check started, or one added or removed. The counts are dashes, out of date, "the project changed after the check yesterday at 3:30 PM", with **Check Every Build**; the old problems aren't put back.
- **Not known:** a result written by another version of the extension, or one that can't be read. Treated as never checked.
- Overdue reviews still go out of date when the day changes, whatever the files say.
- The result is the check's own: what was found, its summary, and when it started. Unsaved changes at the time were read as saved, and the note still says so.

How the comparison is made is the implementor's, within these: it reads modification times, not contents; it runs once when the project's view first needs it, not before the window is usable; and a branch switch, which rewrites files, reads as a change. Say in the pull request what it costs on `docs/`.

**Done when:** in the integration tests, a check, a reload with nothing changed, and the counts are current with their problems in the Problems panel; a check, a file edited on disk, a reload, and they're out of date, with nothing put back; and a result from another version is ignored. `docs/content/editor/sidebar.md` says the check is remembered and when it isn't, and the pull request adds a decision file for keeping it.

**Decided:** by the maintainer on 21 October 2026: the last check's result is kept between sessions. Running the check when VS Code opens was the other option, and isn't taken.

**Needs:** #777, which changes how the check's state is said.

A follow-up to This page and the Project view as 0.4.1 shipped them. **Done when** below is what done looks like, and it's one pull request.

**The problem:** in a dark theme, the sidebar's webview views (This page, the Project view) sit on a neutral gray, `#121212`, instead of the sidebar's color, while the native views beside them (Pages, Content model) show the theme's `sideBar.background`. Seen with Nu Disco Dark, whose sidebar is `#180D2A`: the views are gray, and their sticky section headers, painted with `--vscode-sideBar-background`, are a purple strip across them.

**The cause, verified:** `views.css` sets `color-scheme: light dark` on `:root`, and VS Code's webview host page sets no `color-scheme`. When a frame's color scheme differs from its embedder's, Chromium paints an opaque backdrop of its own behind the frame (`#121212` for dark), so the view's transparent `body` shows that and not the sidebar.
- In Chromium (Playwright), a transparent frame over `#180d2a` reads `#121212` with `:root { color-scheme: light dark }`, and `#180d2a` without it.
- In VS Code, with the Project view showing, **Developer: Open Webview Developer Tools**, then in the view's frame `document.documentElement.style.colorScheme = "normal"`: the gray turns to the sidebar's purple (the maintainer, 21 October 2026).

**What to build:** `views.css` leaves the root's color scheme at `normal`, so the frame stays transparent and the sidebar, or the panel if the view is moved there, shows through. A control that needs the theme's scheme for its native parts, such as the build switch's `<select>` and its dropdown, gets it on the control, from VS Code's body class (`vscode-dark`, `vscode-light`, `vscode-high-contrast`, `vscode-high-contrast-light`); a `color-scheme` on an element doesn't bring the backdrop back.

- The sticky section headers keep an opaque background so rows scrolling under them stay hidden; `--vscode-sideBar-background` is right in the sidebar, which is where the views are contributed.
- `settings.css` and `preview.css` set the same root `color-scheme`, but each paints the editor's background on its `body`, so nothing shows through them; they're left as they are unless the change is the same one line and the tests say they're unchanged.
- The color test's rule holds: every color in `views.css` is a `--vscode-*` variable.

**Done when:** a webview test draws a view in a frame over a colored embedder, with the dark scheme emulated, and reads the embedder's color behind the view's body, not `#121212`, and it fails with the old stylesheet; the build switch's dropdown still draws in the theme's scheme in a dark theme (a screenshot in the pull request, from VS Code); and nothing a reader sees changes in a light theme.

**Decided:** nothing new: the views were always meant to sit on the sidebar's colors (`views.css`: "every color is one of the `--vscode-*` variables VS Code sets").

The first step of [the rest of the cache](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/proposals/cache.md) ("What to build first", 1), and its steel thread: a finding's identity, proven on the report's Problems section. **Done when** below is what done looks like, and it's one pull request.

**What to build:**

- **A finding's identity** (the proposal's "Differences between runs", and Settled 1), in `ascribe-check`, where the baseline will read it too: its check (the slug); its file, from the project's root with `/`; its fingerprint; and its order among findings with the first three alike, from 0, in the file's order. The same finding in several builds is one, as `check` already merges it.
- **The fingerprint** is the first 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the source text of the finding's span, with each run of whitespace read as one space and the ends trimmed; of its line's text when the span is empty. A committed file will hold it (the baseline, next), so the rule is fixed here, and the pull request's decision file states it exactly.
- **The report's history,** `.ascribe/history/report.json`: the last run's day, and the Problems section's findings by identity. Written whole through a rename after each run, as `links.json` is; `--no-history` neither reads nor writes it; only the report's code opens it, which a test holds, as `tests/all/link_cache.rs` does for the links.
- **The Problems section says what changed:** the JSON's `problems` gains `previous_run`, `new`, and `resolved`, as `links` has them (`null` on a first run and with `--no-history`), and `new_items`, the new problems as a capped list of entries. The text says "14 problems, 2 of them new since 9 October; 5 the last report listed are gone" and lists the new ones. Keys are added and none change: the report's JSON is a contract, so the pull request adds its decision file and the schema's new fields.

**The thread, as a test:** two reports on a copy of a project, with a line added above an existing finding and a new finding added below it between them; the second says one problem is new and none are gone. Then the existing finding's text is edited: it reads as one new and one gone.

**Done when:** the thread's test passes; identity has unit tests for whitespace, an empty span, two alike findings in one file, and a finding in two builds; a first run and `--no-history` say nothing about what's new; `docs/content/checks/report.md`'s Problems section says what's new means and how a finding is told from another; and a changelog entry.

**Decided:** the proposal's Settled 1, by the maintainer on 20 October 2026: a finding's identity is the source text of its span. Filing this from the proposal, 21 October 2026.

content.body:
The baseline from [the rest of the cache](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/proposals/cache.md) ("A baseline", and Settled 2 and 3), for the command line. **Done when** below is what done looks like, and it's one pull request.

**What to build:**

- **`ascribe.baseline`,** beside `ascribe.toml`, committed: one line a finding, by the identity #787 adds.
- **`ascribe baseline write`** adds every current advice finding, creating the file; **`ascribe baseline prune`** removes the entries that match nothing. Both take `--format text|json` and exit `0`, or `2` when they can't run. `write` says how many warnings and errors it skipped, and names the step for putting one off: lower the check to advice in `[checks]`, then write again.
- **`ascribe check` reads it:** a finding in it isn't reported, and is counted ("0 errors, 0 warnings, 2 advice, 3,412 in the baseline"), as an acknowledged one is. Only advice is ever held back: an entry whose check a project has since raised to a warning or an error doesn't hide it. `--no-baseline` reports everything.
- **An entry that matches nothing is reported, as advice,** so a stale baseline can't hide a later finding with the same fingerprint: a new diagnostic, added to `tests/conformance/diagnostics.toml` and `diagnostics.rs`, whose fix is `ascribe baseline prune`.
- **`check`'s JSON** gains the count held back, added and changing nothing else.

**The file's syntax, proposed, for the maintainer to approve or change:** it's committed, so it can't change once it ships.

```text
# ascribe baseline 1
# Advice put off for now: ascribe baseline write adds, ascribe baseline prune removes.
# check fingerprint order file
description-too-long 3f9a2c1b9e0d4a77 0 guides/install.md
link-text-generic 91c04e2d7b5a6f18 1 guides/install.md
```

- The first line names the format and its version; `#` starts a comment, and a blank line is ignored.
- Fields are separated by one space. The file is last, so a path with spaces needs no quoting; it's from the project's root, with `/`.
- Lines are sorted by file, then check, then fingerprint, then order, so a file's entries are together, two people adding to it rarely touch the same line, and a diff reads as a list of findings.
- A line that doesn't parse is an error naming the line, and `check` doesn't run with a baseline it can't read.

**Done when:** conformance cases for a finding held back, one not held back because its check is now a warning, a stale entry, and a malformed line; CLI tests for `write`, `prune`, `--no-baseline`, and their JSON; `write` run twice gives the same file byte for byte; the docs have a page for the baseline under `docs/content/checks/`, the commands' reference, and the syntax; `project-docs/surface.md` regenerated; and a changelog entry. The pull request adds a decision file for the command, the file, and its syntax.

**Decided:** the proposal's Settled 2 (advice only) and 3 (`ascribe baseline`, with `write` and `prune`), by the maintainer on 20 October 2026.

**Needs the maintainer:** the syntax above, approved or changed, here. **Needs:** #787.

Piece 1 of [an `ascribe.toml` that says only what's the project's own](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/proposals/shorter-content-model.md#1-frontmatter-every-type-shares), and its steel thread. **Done when** below is what done looks like, and it's one pull request.

**What to build:**
- **`[frontmatter]`,** a top-level table of fields every type has. A type's own `frontmatter` adds fields; a type that declares a field `[frontmatter]` has replaces it whole, for that type (Settled 3). The implicit `page` type of a model with no types has the shared fields too.
- **`title` is implicit:** every type has a required string `title`, declared or not; declaring it changes only how it's read (`inline`). The loader keeps the rule, and `model-type-title` goes.
- **Roles by name:** a field named `description` (string), `review-date` (date), or `owner` (string or enum) takes that role unless the type gives the role to another field.
- **A type with no keys,** `[types.index]`, is valid.
- `[frontmatter]` is a row in the registry (`crates/ascribe-model/settings.toml`), so the reference's tables and Project Settings show it.

**The thread:** `docs/ascribe.toml`'s six types cut down to `[frontmatter]` and each type's `purpose`, `template`, and `guide`, with every output of the docs and of `site/` byte for byte the same (`node scripts/compare/outputs.ts --base main`). The comments stay, reworded for what's now shared.

**Done when:** conformance cases for a shared field, a type that replaces one, the implicit `title` with and without `inline`, each role taken by name, a role given to another field, and an empty type; the thread above; SPEC §7.2 and `docs/content/content-model/index.md` §4 and §5.4 say it; the generated tables rewritten; `model-type-title` removed from `diagnostics.toml` and `diagnostics.rs`; a changelog entry; and a decision file, since SPEC §7.2 is a contract.

Seen on macOS, building the site with Astro. **What happened, and what you expected:** `packages/elements/CONTRACT.md` says an element that holds no markdown, an empty widget among them, "is written as one HTML block" (§0). §5 says an empty widget "is a single line": ``. A single line like that isn't an HTML block in CommonMark: - A custom element isn't one of the names in kind 6. - Kind 7 needs the open tag alone on its line, followed only by whitespace. So a renderer of the site output, such as Astro's, reads the line as inline HTML and wraps it in a paragraph. The landing page in #817 gets `

` for a widget bound to its heading, and `site.css` hides the paragraph to work around it. What I expected: the element is an HTML block on its own, as the contract says. Either: - the emitter writes an empty widget so it starts an HTML block, for example the open tag alone on its line and the closing tag on the next, which kind 7 accepts; or - the contract stops promising a block. Either is a contract change (§0 and §5 of CONTRACT.md, and the fixtures in `tests/render/`), so it needs a recorded decision. `render_site_html` and the Astro plugin must agree on the result. **The smallest input that shows it:** A widget with `binding = "heading"` and no content, as `story-pillar` in `site/home/ascribe.toml` on the `website-phase-2` branch (#817). Build it and render the site Markdown with any CommonMark renderer: the element comes out inside `

`. Found while building the landing page (website plan, phase 2), and noted in `project-docs/brainstorm.md` §18.

content.body:
The nightly canary failed on 22 October, and `next` was left mixing two nights. It's the third time npm has been slow to show a package the canary just published, always `@ascribed/cli-linux-arm64`. This issue is to find out why, and to change the canary so a slow package can't leave `next` split or fail the run. **Done when** below is what done looks like.

**What happened:** [canary run 39755622994](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/actions/runs/39755622994), attempt 1, published all eight packages as `0.4.2-next.29` under `next-pending` between 09:40:22 and 09:41:16 UTC, each `npm publish` succeeding. `tagNpm` in `scripts/release/publish.ts` then moved `next` package by package: `@ascribed/cli-darwin-arm64` at 09:42:32, then it polled `npm view @ascribed/cli-linux-arm64@0.4.2-next.29 --prefer-online` every 10 seconds until its 15-minute deadline, at 09:56:17, and failed. The tags were left split: `cli-darwin-arm64`'s `next` at `next.29`, every other package's, `@ascribed/cli` included, at `next.28`. The daily docs report then ran `@ascribed/cli@next`, a binary from before #807 and #810, against `main`'s `docs/ascribe.toml`, and failed (#830). Re-running the failed job, once every package showed, moved the rest.

**What npm records:** the `time` npm keeps for each version is well after its publish returned:

| Package | `npm publish` returned | npm's `time` for the version | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cli-darwin-arm64` | 09:40:29 | 09:42:13 | 2 min |
| `cli-win32-x64` | 09:40:51 | 09:43:30 | 3 min |
| `cli` | 09:40:57 | 09:44:11 | 3 min |
| `cli-linux-x64` | 09:40:43 | 09:46:55 | 6 min |
| `cli-linux-arm64` | 09:40:36 | 09:57:58 | 17 min |

So the version wasn't in the registry yet when the deadline passed: the delay is npm's processing after it accepts a publish, not a cache in front of it, which `--prefer-online` (989a4cbf) already skips. Size doesn't explain the order (linux-arm64 is 15.9 MB, smaller than linux-x64 and win32-x64).

**Earlier times:** 989a4cbf (5 October), when the check answered from npm's cache; and 2ea7f50b (11 October, [run 38102695001](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/actions/runs/38102695001)), when `cli-linux-arm64@0.2.1-next.13` didn't show within 3 minutes and the deadline went to 15.

**To find out:**
- Why `cli-linux-arm64` is the slow one each time: npm's own processing (a scan, provenance verification), something in that package's tarball or metadata, or chance. npm's status page and the published versions' `time`s across the canaries so far would show whether it's always last.
- Whether `npm dist-tag add` succeeds for a version that `npm view` doesn't show yet, and whether a dist-tag pointing at a version npm hasn't finished is safe for an installer.

**What the canary should do, whatever the cause:** never leave `next` split, and not fail a night for npm's delay. Options to weigh, recommending one in the pull request: wait for every package before tagging any (today it tags as it goes, which is how `next` split); move `next` in a separate job that retries later, or on the next night's run, when `next-pending` is ahead of `next`; or a longer deadline, which only moves the line.

**Done when:** the cause is written down here, as far as it can be found; `tagNpm` moves no package's `next` until every package is on npm; a night whose packages take longer than the wait leaves `next` where it was, all of it, and a later run or a retry moves it; RELEASING.md's nightly canary section says how; and `scripts/release/publish.ts`'s tests cover a package that shows late.

**Done when** below is what done looks like, and it's one pull request.

**The problem:** the extension treats every `ascribe.toml` in the workspace as a project, leaving out only `**/node_modules/**`, what `files.exclude` hides, and `ascribe.projects.exclude` (`projectExclude` in `packages/vscode/src/projects.ts`). In this repository, `cargo test` writes 17 projects into `target/tmp/` (`CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR`), which git ignores; Switch Project listed every one, and each started a language server when a test run rewrote it. A repository fixed it in its own `.vscode/settings.json` (0cd308ce), but every project with a build folder or a dependency folder that holds an `ascribe.toml` hits the same thing first.

**What to build:**

1. **A folder git ignores isn't searched for projects.** In a workspace folder that's a git repository, an `ascribe.toml` that `git check-ignore` reports is left out, as one call with every candidate on standard input (`git check-ignore --stdin`), or through VS Code's Git extension where it's on. VS Code 1.138's stable `workspace.findFiles` doesn't read ignore files, so the extension asks git. Where git isn't there, or the folder isn't a repository, the defaults below still apply. A file that's open still finds its project, as a passed-over project's file does today.
2. **Default patterns, for what's never a project anywhere,** whether or not git ignores it, before `files.exclude` and `ascribe.projects.exclude`:
   - **Ascribe's own:** `.ascribe` (each project's outputs and caches).
   - **Dependencies:** `node_modules` (as now), `bower_components`, `vendor`, `.venv`, `venv`, `__pypackages__`.
   - **Build output and caches whose names are only ever that:** `target`, `dist`, `.output`, `.next`, `.nuxt`, `.svelte-kit`, `.astro`, `.turbo`, `.vercel`, `.netlify`, `.cache`, `coverage`, `.gradle`, `.vscode-test`, `.tox`, `.nox`.
   - Not `build`, `out`, or `bin`: those names are also used for folders people write in, and git's ignore rules cover them where they're output.
3. **A source's copies aren't projects.** A project's copies of another repository's files (SPEC §7.4, `sources/<name>/` in its folder) can hold that repository's own `ascribe.toml`; it's code the project shows, not a project to work on.
4. **`ascribe.projects.exclude`'s description** names the defaults and the git rule, and it stays the way to leave out anything else.

**Done when:** unit tests for the pattern with the defaults; an integration test with a workspace whose `target/` and a git-ignored folder each hold an `ascribe.toml`, neither listed nor started, while a project beside them is; a source's copy left out; the setting's description and `docs/content/editor/` (where projects are found, and Switch Project) say what's left out and how to bring a project back; `project-docs/surface.md` regenerated if the setting's text is in it; and a changelog entry.

**Decided:** by the maintainer on 22 October 2026: default ignored folders, starting from `target/`.

**Done when** below is what done looks like, and it's one pull request.

**The problem:** with `ascribe.startServers` at its default, `onDemand`, a project's language server starts "the first time one of its files is opened, or changes on disk while the window is open". The second half starts servers nobody asked for: a branch switch, a pull, a test run that rewrites fixtures, or an agent editing files can start a server for every project those changes touch, and a server once started runs until the window closes. A server already running still follows changes on disk as it does now.
- **What a project that hasn't started shows** stays as today: no problems in the Problems panel, and "not checked yet" in Switch Project.
- **Stopping an idle server is out of scope here;** say in the pull request whether it's needed after this, with what a session in this repository runs before and after.

Phase 1 of [Embedded help](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/embedded-help/README.md). The plan is [phase-1-thread.md](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/embedded-help/phase-1-thread.md); read it and the README's decisions 1 to 13 and "Rules for every phase" before starting. One pull request. **Needs nothing.**

**What to build:** every build writes `_ascribe/help.json` beside `permalinks.json` (version 1: `version`, `build`, `line`, and `help` keyed by name, each with `title`, `summary`, `text`, `address`, `source`). The section comes from `ascribe-resolve` (decision 6); its `text` comes from the plain renderer's own block loop over that slice, with images as alt text (decision 11); the summary is the first paragraph (decision 10). Aliases and retired permalinks are resolved with code shared with `permalinks.json`. Quill's `prerequisites` and `connect` become permalinks, and `examples/quill/product/help.ts` reads the file and prints a permalink's title, summary, and "Read more". The docs page `docs/content/permalinks/in-your-product.md`, output-layout §1.7, its decision file, and `changes/language/embedded-help.md`.

**Done when:**
- The goal's commands (`ascribe build --config examples/quill`, then `node examples/quill/product/help.ts … prerequisites`, and an unknown name exiting `1`) run in a test.
- The agreement test passes for every project under `examples/` and `tests/conformance/cases/`, and both ways for quill's `prerequisites` and `connect`.
- `crates/ascribe-emit/tests/all/help.rs` covers the cases task 3 lists.
- `node scripts/compare/outputs.ts --base main` changes only `help.json`, the manifests, and quill's `permalinks.json`, each named with `--accept`; every tested output the quill change touches is blessed and read, and the examples observed again.
- The pull request records the docs' own file's measurements: how many permalinks have a summary, the median and longest, how many are over 300 characters, how many have none, and that each diagnostic's is its metadata line. Phases 2 to 4 read them.

**Stop and report** if a section can't be rendered alone and agree with its page (decision 11): that changes the design before anything reads the file.
