content.body:
Phase 2 of [Embedded help](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/embedded-help/README.md). The plan is [phase-2-marker-decision.md](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/embedded-help/phase-2-marker-decision.md), which has the measurements and the full reasoning. A decision by the maintainer, then one pull request with the decision file; no code.

**What #885's measurements show:** no rule over the prose picks a good summary. Of the docs' 326 entries, the 240 diagnostics' first paragraph is their metadata line (155 have a **When** paragraph; 85 have none); 37 sections open with a paragraph over 300 characters whose first sentence would do; 7 open with a lead-in ending in ":"; 2 have no paragraph first. A summary is something a writer, or an agent, decides.

**Recommended, after discussing it with @KyleBlankRollins:** a section summary, `@summary`, for every section, with `@note`'s two bindings (SPEC §4: "self (with primary), else following block"):

```markdown
## `ascribe versions release`
@id {permalink=true}: cli-versions-release

@summary
Releases a line.

It rewrites each mark's `planned` for its target to the line's version, …
```

```markdown
## ASC149 `page-size`
@id {permalink=true}: ASC149
@summary: A page's Markdown, as a build writes it for agents to read, is as long as the limit or longer.
```

- **`@summary` alone** makes the next block the summary, rendered where it is: a writer picks a sentence the page already shows, so nothing is written twice.
- **`@summary: text`** gives its own text, which the page's body doesn't show, as a page's `description` isn't in its body: for a lead-in or a diagnostic.
- **General, not help's:** any section may have one. Embedded help is its first reader; the JSON output, link hovers, search, and link previews can read it later.
- **Optional, and no guessing:** from phase 3, `help.json`'s `summary` is the section's `@summary` or absent; phase 1's first-paragraph rule goes.
- **Not chosen:** a container (`@summary:` … `@end`), a heading attribute naming a paragraph (`summary=2`), and a `{render=true}` attribute, which would make one attribute change both where the text comes from and whether it shows.

**Also settled, as recommended in the plan:** one summary per section (a second is an error); the line form at the top of its section, the following form before the block it marks; the following form marks a paragraph; the line form's text is inline content; a summary in a fragment is its landing section's; one inside a variant arm is an error until phase 6; the line form writes nothing in the site and plain bodies, the following form's block is written as it is with its own source anchors, and the JSON output carries the summary on the section's heading; the generator writes `@summary:` from each diagnostic's `when`, and the 85 without one get a `when`.

**The one question left for @KyleBlankRollins:** the check for a section with a permalink and no summary. Summaries aren't tied to permalinks; only this check ties them, and only for embedded help. Recommended: **advice by default, configurable in `[checks]`**, so a project that only links to its permalinks isn't asked for summaries, and one that ships embedded help raises it to a warning.

**Done when:** a decision file in `project-docs/decisions/`, numbered by this issue, records the form, each rule, the check's default, and why, and nothing else changes. #880 (phase 3) starts from it.

**Blocked by #878 and #879.** The directive's bindings and rules are whatever #879's decision file settles; don't choose them here.

**What to build:** `@summary`, general to every section, with both bindings (`@summary: text`, its own text not shown in the body; `@summary` alone, the next block, rendered where it is), through syntax, `fmt`, resolve, and the site, plain, and JSON emitters, with its diagnostics. `help.rs` takes the summary from the section's `@summary`, or leaves it absent: decision 10's first-paragraph rule is removed, and `help.json`'s keys don't change. The language server's completion and hover for it. The diagnostics generator writes `@summary: <when>` under each diagnostic's `@id`, and each of the 85 diagnostics without a `when` gets one in `diagnostics.toml`; if those sentences make the pull request too large to read, they go first, in a pull request of their own.

**Done when:**
- After `ascribe build --config docs`, every diagnostic's `help.json` summary is its `when`, and no entry's summary comes from a section without `@summary`.
- Conformance cases for both bindings' parse and canonical form, a summary in a fragment, in a variant arm, two in a section, and each diagnostic; emit tests for each binding, a fragment, and none.
- Site and plain outputs of every project are byte for byte the same where no `@summary` is written; the diagnostics reference's changes are its `@summary` lines and new `when` sentences, named with `--accept`.

- **The editor:** the hover on a section's heading and its `@id` line, and This page's Permalink row tooltip, show the section's summary, from the function `help.rs` uses.

content.body:
Phase 7 of [Embedded help](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/embedded-help/README.md). The plan is [phase-7-agents.md](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/embedded-help/phase-7-agents.md). One pull request.

**Blocked by #878** (`help.rs`'s entry function). Independent of phases 2 to 6; after #880 its summaries are the marked ones with nothing to change here.

**What to build:** `go:<name>` in `resolve`'s page argument names a permalink (decision 15). The text output is the title, the summary when there is one, the text, and "Read more" with the address; `--format json` is the entry as `help.json` writes it, with `version`, `build`, and `line`, from `help.rs`'s function. An unknown name exits `1` with the closest names; a retired one gives its reason. `ascribe_resolve` takes the same `go:<name>`. The rules `ascribe agents sync` writes say a product's message can read what the docs will show with `ascribe resolve go:<name>`.

**Done when:**
- `ascribe resolve go:prerequisites --build site --config examples/quill` prints the goal's output, in a CLI test, with its JSON, an unknown name, and a retired one; outputs in `crates/ascribe-cli/tests/output/`, observed again.
- `ascribe_resolve` with `go:` in the MCP tests; the rules' sentence in the agents' tests.
- `resolve`'s reference and JSON contract, the embedded help page, a decision file for `go:` and the JSON, `changes/command/resolve-permalink.md`, the surface map.
